title: Barcelona midfielder eyeing special milestone against Valencia
description: Rodri’s inclusion into Hansi Flick’s plans has been measured and cautious, for the manager is aware of the player’s fitness struggles and recent injury history.When fit, there is no doubt that t...
fullText:
Rodri's inclusion into Hansi Flick's plans has been measured and cautious, for the manager is aware of the player's fitness struggles and recent injury history.

When fit, there is no doubt that the new Barcelona signing is one of the best players in the world, and the club plans to manage his minutes effectively to keep him fit for the big games.

So far, Rodri has made two appearances for Barcelona in La Liga and came off the bench on both nights. Tomorrow, he will make his third appearance for the Catalans as they take on Valencia, and it will be a very special occasion for him if he does so.

Rodri's career in La Liga began at Villarreal, and he then moved to Atletico Madrid for a brief period before signing for Manchester City and kicking off a legendary spell at the English club.

A special occasion awaits Rodri. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Tomorrow, he will make his 100th appearance in La Liga marking a special milestone in his career in Spain.

Rodri made 63 appearances with Villarreal after his debut in the 2015-16 campaign and then made 34 appearances for Atletico Madrid after he signed for them in the 2018-19 campaign.

Adding his two Barcelona appearances so far in the league, he stands on 99 games.

If Flick hands him any minutes tomorrow, he will reach the three-digit mark in terms of appearances in the Spanish league in which he has four goals and five assists to his name.

Both of the former Ballon d'Or winner's appearances for Barcelona so far have come off the bench, and it is clear that the manager is being cautious with their incorporation.

Will Flick start Rodri? (Photo by Timothy Rogers/Getty Images)

Yet, it is clear that Rodri has significantly helped Barcelona's in-game dominance whenever called-on, making him a valuable asset as a starting piece already.

The player is still waiting for his first start in a Barcelona shirt, and there is a chance tomorrow is that big day.

However, there is also a high possibility that Hansi Flick prefers to wait it out a couple more days and start a fully fit Rodri in Barcelona's first UEFA Champions League game of the season.

title: Marcus Rashford celebrates Man United return with special tribute
description: 1Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford has hinted at his stance on wearing the No. 9 shirt at Old Trafford. The English forward was handed the iconic shirt this summer after returning from his tem...
fullText:
Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford has hinted at his stance on wearing the No. 9 shirt at Old Trafford. The English forward was handed the iconic shirt this summer after returning from his temporary spell with Barcelona.

Rashford spent last season on loan at Camp Nou and was expected to permanently join the LaLiga champions this summer. The Englishman was a hit with the Catalans, scoring 14 goals and registering 15 assists during his stay.

However, Barcelona performed a U-turn and signed Anthony Gordon instead, opting against triggering an option to make Rashford's stay permanent. The Englishman was subsequently reintegrated into the Red Devils' squad and even featured in pre-season with his new shirt number.

Rashford began the Premier League season from the bench, coming on at the break in the 2-0 defeat to Hull City. The Englishman started the 5-2 win over Ipswich Town last weekend and had a decent outing.

Rashford first wore the No. 9 shirt during his time with the United Under-18 team. During his stint with the Under-21s, the Englishman switched between numbers 16, 15, 14, 10, and 9.

When he broke into the first team under former manager Louis van Gaal in the 2015/16 season, Rashford donned the No. 39 shirt. The Englishman had an explosive entry into the senior side, scoring a brace in his senior debut against Midtjylland in the Europa League and another brace in his Premier League debut against Arsenal.

It was clear that the Red Devils had a gem in their hands, with Rashford moving to the No. 19 the following campaign. The player took over the No. 10 shirt in the summer of 2018, after Zlatan Ibrahimovic's exit, and wore that number right until his fallout with former head coach Ruben Amorim in December 2024.

He moved to Aston Villa in January 2025 on a six-month loan, and wore the No. 9 shirt at Villa Park. At Barcelona, the 28 year old wore the fabled No. 14, before returning to the No. 9 this season. For the record, Matheus Cunha has been wearing the No. 10 for the Red Devils since last season.

The Englishman has now paid tribute to his recent shirt numbers with a special gesture.

Rashford has added two new shirt numbers to his tattoo collection. The Englishman already had the shirt numbers 39, 10, and 19 inked on his body and has now added 14 and 9 to the set.

Sharing the news on Instagram, he wrote: "New number, Same mission…"

Rashford follows in the footsteps of legendary strikers at Old Trafford who donned the No. 9, including Andy Cole, Mark Hughes and Dennis Law. Rasmus Hojlund was the last player to wear the number for United, before leaving for Napoli last summer.

Rashford has scored 138 goals and registered 79 assists in 428 appearances in all competitions for United to date. The Englishman has the chance to add to that tally this season, and perhaps salvage his career at the Theatre of Dreams.

We'll find out when Man City hosts Coventry City on Saturday at the Etihad Stadium. The Argentina international hasn't had much time to work with his new teammates, but he's familiar to manager Enzo Maresca, who worked with Fernandez at Chelsea before his departure.

Now, taking over for legendary City manager Pep Guardiola, the Italian boss may be tempted to give him an early opportunity against a Coventry side looking for its first point since returning to the top division. Manager Frank Lampard told USA TODAY Sports before the season that he was ready for a tough start to the season, opening with trips to Arsenal and Manchester City, but felt his team could compete.

City will be without winger Jeremy Doku, who is still dealing with a calf injury, but Maresca can otherwise call on a team full of stars including forward Erling Haaland, who scored twice in last week's win over Crystal Palace, and Rayan Cherki.

title: Duleep Trophy final comes at right time for Mohammed Siraj to find rhythm
description: Mohammed Siraj and Devdutt Padikkal have been included in the South Zone squad for the Duleep Trophy final. With Siraj's recent performance and heavy workload drawing scrutiny, he managed just two wickets in his last Test against Sri Lanka. Former selector Devang Gandhi has urged Siraj to leverage his experience wisely, emphasizing his ability to generate wobble seam as a significant asset.
fullText:
Chennai: The Duleep Trophy final got a boost of stardom with paceman Mohammed Siraj and left-hander Devdutt Padikkal joining the South Zone squad. For Siraj, the domestic assignment comes at a time when questions over his form, wicket-taking impact and workload have begun to gather momentum.

TOI understands that Siraj's place came under scrutiny after the first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle, with the team management considering Gurnoor Brar for the second Test in Colombo. Siraj eventually retained his place, but in the 26 overs that he bowled in the drawn game, he could manage only two wickets.

Former national selector and India opener Devang Gandhi said this is where Siraj should bring his experience into play.

"I have seen Mohammed Shami from close quarters. In the second session, his pace normally used to drop, but that was often deliberate. He used to soften up the batter and then suddenly bowl that killer delivery. So when you grow a little older, it's not always about going flat out but being judicious about it," Gandhi said, adding that Siraj has everything in his armoury that should help him roar back.

"His biggest asset is his ability to bowl with wobble seam. When a bowler does that, the ball tends to seam depending on which side of the seam it lands. That's something he should never lose," Gandhi added.

title: Newcastle United v Bournemouth preview ahead of today’s St James’ Park match
description: Welcome to the Newcastle United v Bournemouth preview. Saturday 5th September and a 12.
fullText:
Welcome to the Newcastle United v Bournemouth preview.

Saturday 5th September and a 12.30pm kick-off.

Newcastle United have the opportunity to go top of the league by 2.30pm when facing Bournemouth at home in their fourth straight televised fixture.

The Toon will be looking to continue their unbeaten start to the season in front of an expectant home crowd.

Whilst Bournemouth will be looking to get their campaign back on track following late heartbreak against both Man City and Everton.

Newcastle are enjoying a fine start to the season and are unbeaten in their three matches so far.

If they were disappointed to be robbed of two points on the opening day of the season then they didn't show it when following this up with a 3-2 win in the League Cup. Even better was to follow a few days later when Tottenham Hotspur were put to the sword in a cracking away performance. We've scored seven goals so far and conceded four.

Bournemouth have only taken one point from their first two matches but that doesn't begin to tell the tale of five points dropped from winning positions. A tremendous effort away at Man City saw the cherries 1-0 up for the vast majority of the match before succumbing to two goals in the last few minutes to lose 2-1. A similar story at home to Everton saw Bournemouth on course for victory until conceding in the ninety-first minute to turn three points into one. They've scored two goals so far and conceded three.

The Toon travelled to Tottenham on Saturday evening and produced a tremendous 2-0 win. The first hour was a nervy affair with NUFC being grateful for a number of fine Hornicek saves before the move of the match put United ahead. A fabulous ball out of defence from Gonzalez on his debut allowed Dedic to head the ball in the path of Elanga who took a touch and turned before slamming the ball home off the post. More of this please!

Ten minutes later, a Lewis Hall corner was headed on by Woltemade for Wissa to flick home with his back to goal and send the away fans wild! Elanga has continued his brilliant start to the season and the new boys are already settling in well. It's still early days for our new manager and important to stay grounded but the opening three matches have promised the start of something very special indeed.

Bournemouth hosted Everton last weekend and were devastated to once again concede a costly injury-time goal. Despite Everton having the better of the match, it was Bournemouth closing in on a crucial victory before conceding a ninety-first equaliser meaning they had to be content with a point.

-Eight Premier League matches between the two sides at St James' Park have seen two Newcastle wins, two draws and four defeats.

-Bournemouth have visited St James Park for two recent cup matches. United winning 1-0 in the League Cup in December 2022 on the way to Wembley and victorious on penalties in January 2026 in the FA Cup.

-The last four matches between the two sides on Tyneside has seen an astonishing eighteen goals.

In 2018, Rafa Benitez and his Toon side were hoping for a win against Bournemouth to achieve back-to-back Premier League victories for the first time all season. Thankfully this was the match that striker Salomon Rondon decided to announce his arrival at St James' Park with a match-winning display. The game was only seven minutes old when he fired in a loose ball at the back post. Even better was to come near the end of the half when Kenedy swung in a cross from the left and Rondon did his best Sir Les impression to smash a header into the top corner and put the Toon 2-0 up. Bournemouth were able to pull one back due to an assist from future Newcastle player Ryan Fraser but Rondon continued to terrorise the Bournemouth defence forcing a number of fine saves and being desperately unlucky not to complete a hat-trick in a fine win for the Toon. Newcastle 2-1 Bournemouth.

Christian Atsu made his Newcastle United debut in 2016 and was a crucial part of the team that won the Championship under Rafa Benitez who soon made his loan move from Chelsea permanent. He stayed at the Toon for five years, making over one-hundred appearances and scoring eight league goals. Previous to his time at NUFC, he was on loan for a season at Bournemouth but only made two League Cup appearances in a frustrating spell with the Cherries. Sadly, 2023 brought the devastating news that Atsu had passed away in the aftermath of an earthquake in Turkey leaving behind a wife and three young children. Rest In Peace.

Freddie Woodman played four league games for Steve Bruce at the start of the 21/22 season. Unfortunately, this coincided with three defeats and a draw with Woodman heavily criticised for his part in a 4-1 defeat at Old Trafford. He was demoted to the bench and then loaned to Bournemouth where he played just one match for the Cherries.

Matt Ritchie played for Bournemouth between 2012 and 2016 and scored thirty-one goals for the Cherries. In 14/15 he was voted the football league's player of the season in a poll by 'Four Four Two' magazine. He signed for the Toon in 2016 and became an integral part of our midfield as we achieved promotion back to the Premier League under Rafa Benitez. He stayed for eight years and scored twenty-five goals. His last goal for the club came in injury time against Bournemouth as he rescued a 2-2 draw and celebrated in his usual style by booting the corner flag.

Matthias Jaissle after a 2-0 win away at Tottenham:

"Incredible, I'm really proud. We are really proud as a club and coaching staff to see a team on the pitch delivering already on a high level, totally committed to what we are doing. This is a good start so I'm really, really proud and it's a moment to enjoy. We did well also last week. This was another step in the right direction against a strong opponent with huge signings during the window. This was something we were aware of but how we handled that challenge was amazing. We're really pleased, not only because of the goals we scored but because of the performance and how we improved during the match. That should give us confidence to be able to adjust things and that's what the lads showed, especially in the second half."

Marco Rose after a 1-1 draw at home to Everton:

"It was a quite open game, quite up and down. We can get better in some parts of the game. It was not even a set piece for the goal because we had already cleared the situation, but I don't want to blame anyone because I saw so many positive things. I am really thankful for the warm welcome and I really appreciate being coach of this team. Like last week, we would like to present our fans with a win, but we will have to wait one more week."

Newcastle United fans food bank will once again be collecting opposite the Gallowgate end and gratefully receiving food, money and toiletries for those in need. Of particular interest are non-perishable food and drink items (such as noodles, pasta, rice, canned food, soup, cereal, cordial, long life milk etc) as well as toiletries such as shower gel, shampoo, toothpaste and sanitary products. Please give whatever you can, any donation is very much appreciated.

For further info and/or to donate online go to Newcastle Foodbank

Expectations have been raised by Newcastle's excellent start to the season under Matthias Jaissle.

Anyone expecting a walk in the park this weekend mind could be in for a rude awakening. Bournemouth have been desperately unlucky not to take maximum points in both of their matches and will be desperate for a win. It's always difficult to predict an early kick-off and I think we're in for an even match. I think it'll be 0-0 at half-time but we'll have just enough to get the win over the line with two second-half strikes. Newcastle 2-1 Bournemouth.

Join Jamie, Simon and Hutch as they take a deep dive into everything Newcastle United.

title: Three things to watch as UWF football faces first Division I road test
description: After a stunning upset win, UWF football hits the road to face No. 24 Central Arkansas. Here's what to watch in the matchup.
fullText:
When UWF football head coach Kaleb Nobles turns on the film for No. 24 Central Arkansas, one thing stands out immediately. It has nothing to do with the personnel on the field.

"T purple and gray turf that's for sure," Nobles said. "You see it on film, you cannot miss it. It is an awesome field, it is a good environment. I've never been there for a game so we'll find out Saturday what it'll look like. I'm sure it'll be rocking."

The two teams will kick off at Estes Stadium in Conway, Arkansas on Sept. 5 at 6 p.m. Like UWF, Central Arkansas also upset a top 25 team in Week 0, knocking off No. 22 Tennessee-Martin 36-24 on the road.

This will not only be UWF's first road game as a Division I team, but its United Athletic Conference opener too.

Here's three things to watch in this one.

UWF fans haven't come down from the Argos 34-31 win over No. 16 Southern Illinois on Aug. 27, but the focus among the team itself since the end of last weekend has been Central Arkansas.

After watching his team come out, play with energy and continue to fight even through adversity, Nobles liked a couple other things on film too. The Argos played just five offensive linemen, but they were in sync throughout the game and helped UWF run for 226 yards and only give up one sack. He also liked how receivers and tight ends were making blocks in the open field after the initial hole was opened up.

The kicking game was solid too, as UWF hit all its extra points.

But as always, especially in Week 1, there are things to improve. Nobles thought redshirt sophomore quarterback Ty'ray Davis was a little antsy early in his first start, but that's to be expected in that environment. Davis finished his first start completing seven of 17 passes for 109 yards and two touchdowns and ran for 88 yards and a touchdown.

The Argos defense tired as the game went on after holding its own in the first half, allowing 403 yards as it struggled to stop SIU's up-tempo offense. For Nobles, that comes down to making plays when they're in position to be made.

UWF doesn't have all offseason to prepare for Central Arkansas like they did Southern Illinois, but the Bears are in the same boat. Both teams played on Thursday, which means equal time to prepare and take more steps to what Nobles calls "playing great football."

"A lot of good things, some bad things we gotta fix," Nobles said. "Because we know Central Arkansas's got a good staff that's looking to expose some of that stuff.

The most glaring issue from UWF's season-opening win were the giveaways. The Argos fumbled the ball four times, losing three that led to 18 points for SIU.

The two second half fumbles let the Salukis back into the game. The Argos led 27-9 with 5:43 left in the third quarter before Cannon Brite coughed it up and the Salukis marched down the field for a touchdown to cut the lead to 27-17.

Then Keishawn Smith fumbled with 12:04 left in the fourth quarter and Southern Illinois scored another touchdown to cut the Argos lead to 27-24 with 7:32 left.

If not for the first fumble, UWF could've put the game away on that drive. Instead, it went down to the wire. The Argos defense forced four turnovers of its own, but that formula on both sides of the ball isn't sustainable.

"I think just pushing these guys to understand when you get opportunities late in the game to put somebody away," Nobles said. "You gotta do that because that gives you a better chance at the end of the game to not coast, but you ain't got to stress as much."

Both teams will be looking to build off statement Week 0 wins. Just like the Argos, the Bears got off to an unexpected start, upsetting a ranked team after going 3-9 in 2025.

Sophomore quarterback Donovyn Omolo threw for 243 yards and three touchdowns and ran for 118 yards. Arlie Lee caught a 19-yard touchdown with 27 seconds left in the second quarter to put UCA up 19-17, then a 51-yard bomb from Omolo in the third quarter to make it a two-possession game.

Junior linebacker Ashtyn Williams recorded a team-high 16 tackles and redshirt freshman Bryson Adamoh and junior Jacob Sekiyoba intercepted passes.

Nobles has experience with Omolo, as he transferred from Central Missouri and showed up on Delta State film when the Argos were trying to prepare for the Statesmen last year. UWF also did a walkthrough at Estes Stadium on their way to playing Northeastern State last fall.

"(Omolo's) a left handed guy, really quick," Nobles said. "Fast release, he's a quick. They use a little bit of a quarterback draw game so you gotta try and make him beat you on the outside…running backs are good, (offensive) line is pretty big, tight ends are really good players. Defensive side of the ball, decent amount of returners, good (defensive) linemen. They'll mix it up, three-man, four-man front, secondary's really good on the back end. We're going to have to play another tough game."

title: Commanders release former 49ers' second-round pick as comeback falls short
description: Commanders officially move on from former 49ers' second-round pick.
fullText:
The Washington Commanders have dealt with several injuries throughout training camp. Laremy Tunsil's torn triceps has received the most attention. Former second-round pick Johnny Newton tore his pec, while other Washington players, including quarterback Marcus Mariota and center Nick Allegretti, dealt with nagging injuries.

One injury that flew under the radar was linebacker/defensive end Drake Jackson. Washington placed Jackson on the reserve/injured list on Aug. 25, and a little over a week later, the NFL's transaction wire revealed that the Commanders released Jackson with an injury settlement.

Could this be the end of the line for the 25-year-old former 49ers' second-round pick?

Jackson entered the NFL with great promise in 2022, appearing in 15 games for San Francisco and recording three sacks in a limited role. His fortunes began to change in 2023, when he was placed on IR in November after eight games. He returned in 2024, but suffered a torn patellar tendon in training camp. He would miss all of the 2024 season, and the 49ers waived him in May 2025.

Washington was a natural landing spot for Jackson. It needed help at edge rusher. And general manager Adam Peters was the 49ers' assistant GM when they drafted Jackson. So Peters monitored his progress and eventually signed him on Oct. 15. The Commanders immediately placed Jackson on IR, designating him for a return. On Dec. 4, they activated him. He appeared in three games last season, recording three tackles.

The Commanders needed to upgrade the edge rusher position in the offseason, which is what they did by signing Odafe Oweh and K'Lavon Chaisson and using a fifth-round pick on Joshua Josephs. Still, Peters re-signed Jackson to a one-year deal, giving him a chance to earn a spot.

It was a quiet summer for Jackson, while others at this position thrived. Now, he'll look for another opportunity elsewhere, as he's free to sign with another team.

title: Fenerbahce's Guendouzi banned for 2 Champions League games after heated clashes in playoff at Lyon
description: Mattéo Guendouzi was banned by UEFA from Fenerbahce’s first two Champions League games for provocations and insults in a heated playoff win at Lyon in his native France.  Guendouzi, a former player at Lyon’s great rival Marseille, was at the heart of incidents before and after Fenerbahce’s 2-1 win on Aug. 26 including a mass brawl.  The result sent the Turkish club into the Champions League for the first time in 18 years.
fullText:
NYON, Switzerland (AP) — Mattéo Guendouzi was banned by UEFA from Fenerbahce's first two Champions League games for provocations and insults in a heated playoff win at Lyon in his native France.

Guendouzi, a former player at Lyon's great rival Marseille, was at the heart of incidents before and after Fenerbahce's 2-1 win on Aug. 26 including a mass brawl. The result sent the Turkish club into the Champions League for the first time in 18 years.

The 27-year-old Guendouzi will miss Fenerbahce hosting Roma next Thursday and a visit to Aston Villa on Oct. 14.

Fenerbahce forward Mason Greenwood had a one-game ban deferred for one year of probation for his involvement, UEFA said in disciplinary verdicts announced late Friday.

Lyon goalkeeper coach Antonio Ferreira was banned from three Europa League games, with two more games deferred, for "serious assault." He aimed a leaping kick at Guendouzi in a post-game clash near the players' tunnel.

The charges against Guendouzi were violating rules of decent conduct, "insulting players or others present at the match" and provoking spectators, UEFA said.

Guendouzi was fined 50,000 euros ($58,000) and Greenwood, who faced a violation of decent conduct charge, must pay 30,000 euros ($35,000).

Guendouzi raised his middle fingers to Lyon fans during the warmup and after the game, and shouted "Allez l'OM" ("Go Marseille"), while also grabbing his crotch in wild post-match scenes. He later said Lyon fans insulted his family before and during the game.

Guendouzi and Greenwood both joined Fenerbahce in the offseason as part of a big investment by the Istanbul club which has fallen behind city rival Galatasaray in recent years. Galatasaray also will play in the Champions League.

UEFA also fined Fenerbahce 50,000 euros ($58,000) for violating rules of decent conduct and 45,000 euros ($52,000) for fan misconduct.

Lyon was fined 108,500 euros ($126,000) on a series of charges. The team starts in the second-tier Europa League at Anderlecht next Thursday.

title: Browns QB Deshaun Watson has the job but draws a quiet no-confidence vote over Sanders
description: Todd Monken handed Deshaun Watson the Browns' starting job over Shedeur Sanders, but a beat reporter says the seat won't stay his for long.
fullText:
Browns QB Deshaun Watson has the job but draws a quiet no-confidence vote over Sanders originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Deshaun Watson has Cleveland's quarterback job, and almost nobody around the team is treating it as a real endorsement. Todd Monken named the veteran his Week 1 starter over Shedeur Sanders, then spent the rollout insisting the fan reaction and one ugly preseason night played no part in it.

The trouble is that everything surrounding the decision points the other way. The reps, the booing, and the beat all read like doubt, even as the depth chart reads Watson.

The case against him is not hard to assemble. Across 19 games since his 2022 arrival, the three-time Pro Bowler owns a 9-10 record, 19 touchdown passes, 12 interceptions, and an 80.7 rating on 3,365 yards.

He has not thrown a regular-season pass since tearing his Achilles in October 2024. When he took the field at home in the preseason, the crowd booed him, and Watson called the reaction "a little bit more personal than that."

Sanders, meanwhile, gave fans a reason to push for him. He went 3-4 across seven starts as a rookie, completing 56.6 percent of his throws for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 interceptions. That was enough to make him the popular pick to unseat Watson this summer.

Monken went the other way anyway and now runs Sanders with the scout team. The decision is official. The confidence behind it is the part still in question.

The loudest signal that Cleveland's order might not hold came from someone who watched it up close. Daryl Ruiter, appearing on 92.3 The Fan, said the two quarterbacks looked nearly even through camp, which is not what you want to hear about a starter the team just committed to.

"I just didn't see much separation between the two guys," Ruiter said. He added, "I think that Deshaun is more ready to play than Shedeur. But I think Shedeur, by the time we get into the season here, that can change. I think Shedeur will be ready to play, and ultimately this thing's going to get turned over to him at some point, for one reason or another."

That closing line is the whole no-confidence vote in a sentence. Ruiter is not betting on a clean benching over film. He is leaving the door open for the thing that has defined Watson's Browns run: availability. A quarterback rebuilding from an Achilles tear and carrying a long stretch of missed time holds his job on health as much as production.

There is a third arm worth tracking, too. Rookie Taylen Green flashed real ability in the preseason finale against New England, and his Arkansas tape backs it up.

He piled up 2,714 passing yards and 777 rushing yards last season while accounting for 27 total touchdowns. That dual-threat profile could shove him into the backup conversation before long. The job is Watson's today. Almost nobody expects it to stay that way.

title: CTA considers referee decision to not retake Mbappe’s penalty vs Real Betis was right
description: A lot has been said about Real Madrid’s failure to take three points against Real Betis last night, for it marked the team’s first defeat under Jose Mourinho this season.Los Verdiblancos took the ...
fullText:
A lot has been said about Real Madrid's failure to take three points against Real Betis last night, for it marked the team's first defeat under Jose Mourinho this season.

Los Verdiblancos took the lead late on the night, forcing Real Madrid into a position where they had to score twice in ten minutes to take home a win. Vinicius Jr. won a penalty in extra-time, and that handed the visitors their best chance of levelling the scores.

Mbappe's effort, however, was saved by Alvaro Valles cleanly but there was significant controversy over the position of Real Betis player Marc Bartra who seemingly entered the box before Mbappe struck the ball.

A lot has been made about whether the decision not to retake the spot-kick was right or not, but Mundo Deportivo now bring to light that the CTA believes that the verdict was correct.

As reported by the Spanish outlet, the IFAB and the CARD rules are the two important rulebooks that influence referees' decisions.

According to the IFAB rules, a penalty must be retaken for encroachment if the defending team's player directly affects the penalty taker through his encroachment, plays the ball or challenges an opponent.

Further, it then states that if a player is in the air, as Bartra was, the position must be determined by the projected position of their feet if they were touching the ground. That, however, only applies when the player's entire body is in the air.

The CTA's CARD manual, meanwhile, has similar regulations and stipulates that a penalty must be retaken for an encroaching defender only if it directly affects the taker or makes an effort for the ball or challenges an attacking team player.

Real Madrid suffered their first loss. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images)

Considering the rules in both manuals, Mbappe's penalty would only have to be retaken if Bartra's encroachment directly affected Mbappe's penalty, his effort to go for the rebound or made any challenge on a Real Madrid player.

The Real Betis star, however, did none of that and did not even contact the ball immediately after the penalty.

His position may be controversial, but he did not affect Real Madrid's chances at a rebound in any capacity.

In that sense, the decision not to retake the penalty was the right one, and the CTA consider that the officials were right with their verdict.

title: Christopher Bell Goes From Fearing Season-Ending Injury to NASCAR Championship Contender
description: Christopher Bell shared his thoughts on the scary crash at Michigan that nearly ended his title bid. The Joe Gibbs Racing driver has now made the Chase as the sixth seed.
fullText:
Christopher Bell shared his thoughts on the scary crash at Michigan that nearly ended his title bid. The Joe Gibbs Racing driver has now made the Chase as the sixth seed.

Bell experienced a horrifying crash at Michigan when Chase Elliott made contact with the No.20 Toyota. Bell crashed into the outside walls and recorded the biggest change in velocity in the Next Gen era.

The 31-year-old had fractured his left wrist and was seen leaving the venue with a cast. Many feared he'd have to sit out the following races, but Bell returned to race at Pocono with a heavy arm cast.

"I remember at Michigan, in the infield care center, like I thought that number one, my season could be over and number two, my playoff chances are probably over. So then, whenever we got back and I found out that I didn't have to have surgery and the likelihood of me racing the following week was higher, I'm like, 'okay, well, maybe I'll be able to, you know, still fight for a Chase position,'" Bell said in an interview during a Chase media day.

"I think at that time, I was 12th in points or something like that. So I was literally worried about making the chase, making the playoffs. So to be sitting here in 6th in points and still be in contention is something that I'm really proud of," he added.

Christopher Bell sustained a non-displaced fracture that didn't require surgery. He was given a six-week timeline under normal healing conditions. Bell largely drove one-handed and soon transitioned to a splint while racing at Chicagoland Speedway.

Notably, Bell finished runner-up at Chicago, a feat he would repeat three times in the following weeks. Those results helped him finish the regular season near his JGR teammates, who all rank inside the top-5.

The regular-season finale at Daytona was one of the two races where Christopher Bell finished outside the top 10 in the last nine races. It was also the race where NASCAR introduced a new rules package to reduce drag on a lower horsepower setup.

Bell, however, wasn't appreciative of the update.

"It wasn't any different at all, which I was really disappointed in because I really bought into it. I thought it was going to be a lot different and it didn't play out differently at all … Cars drove the exact same," he said via Peter Stratta's X handle.

Christopher Bell ultimately finished 17th and lost his top-5 standing at Daytona. His teammate Chase Briscoe took his spot instead.

Bell now enters the Chase with a 50-point deficit to season leader Denny Hamlin.

title: “There are Survivors in Football”: Shannon Sharpe Calls Out Cam Skattebo After Giants RB’s Retirement Admission
description: On Thursday, Cam Skattebo admitted that he had considered retirement a month into his ankle injury last year. This was just a few months into his NFL career, with the former Arizona State running back having been drafted by the New York Giants in 2025.
fullText:
On Thursday, Cam Skattebo admitted that he had considered retirement a month into his ankle injury last year. This was just a few months into his NFL career, with the former Arizona State running back having been drafted by the New York Giants in 2025.

The admission came in an interview earlier this week in 'Up&Adams' in which the running back spoke about a promise he made to himself in college regarding retiring at the first sign of serious injury. Skattebo also spoke about how the injury allowed him to get to know himself better.

This candid moment by Skattebo caught some by surprise, including Hall of Famer Shannon Sharpe, who was taken aback by the idea that a single injury could take such a toll on a player's confidence. He said as much on Friday's edition of 'Nightcap':

"There are no winners in football; there are survivors in football. You play probably the sports that the most serious injuries happen… You gotta know when the journey is over," said Sharpe

Sharpe and his co-hosts, former NFL player Chad Johnson and former NBA player Joe Johnson, were surprised by the idea that a young player would contemplate retirement shortly after their debut. They saw it as a failure of mentality, at a moment when Skattebo should've been focused on returning to the field with the New York Giants.

Speaking on Thursday in Up&Adams, Cam Skattebo explained that he briefly considered leaving the NFL after his serious ankle injury last year. For him, it was all down to a promise he made to himself before making the jump to the pros. He wouldn't let the NFL get in the way of his health:

"Coming out of college and going into the NFL, I think I gave myself one rule and it was if I ever got a major injury I was done playing," he said. "And that happened seven games into my career, so it kind of sucked."

He also explained that in the end, the recovery process allowed him to get to know himself better:

"Just finding who I was, finding my happiness, finding the person I wanted to be on and off the field. And I think that's something I built over the last nine, 10 months and being able to now focus back on football,"

Nonetheless, Cam Skattebo did say that the recovery process did take a heavy mental toll on him, with days in which he would spend up to 14 hours doing absolutely nothing.

title: How long is Indiana football's home winning streak
description: Indiana football has become unbeatable at home under coach Curt Cignetti. A look at the nation's longest home win streak:
fullText:
BLOOMINGTON — Indiana football coach Curt Cignetti told reporters this week that the environment at Memorial Stadium is worth at least 14 points.

The No. 6 Hoosiers success under Cignetti has transformed the venue into one of the toughest places to play in the country and the numbers back it up.

More: Why Urban Meyer believes Indiana football has key advantage in quest for repeat titles

Under Cignetti, Indiana football is 15-0 in home games. The program's 15-game home win streak is a program record and the nation's longest such streak. The programs with the next longest home win streak are Ohio (13 games) and Ole Miss (11 games).

The Hoosiers have won at home by a wide margin throughout Cignetti's tenure as well. They have all but one game by double digits — a 20-15 win over Michigan in 2024 — and have an average margin of victory of 37.9 points.

Indiana hasn't dropped a game at Memorial Stadium since a 24-21 loss to Michigan State in 2023.

More: Big Noon crew praises IU football's blueprint for developing transfer QBs

The Hoosiers sold out all eight home games they have on their schedule for 2026. The game against North Texas is the first non-conference matchup to sell out at Memorial Stadium since 2021.

It's only the second time in program history IU has sold out all of its home games.

Since the venue expanded in 1970, Indiana has sold out 26 games, with eight of those coming in the last two years.

More: How Indiana football QB Josh Hoover found his way back to Bloomington

The Hoosiers are 27-2 with Cignetti as coach with the most wins of any team in the FBS during the stretch and tied for the fewest losses. Ohio State and Oregon have the next best record from 2024-25 at 26-2.

Indiana has never won more games over a two-year stretch in program history. The team twice won 16 games over two years, 1944-45 and 1987-88.

Cignetti, who has a career record of 146-37, has never had a losing season in 14 seasons as coach. He already ranks eighth in program history in wins.

Michael Niziolek is the Indiana beat reporter for The Bloomington Herald-Times. You can follow him on X @michaelniziolek.

title: Eyes on big prize as Swansea and Wrexham collide
description: Swansea City and Wrexham meet in a mouthwatering Welsh derby with stakes high as both clubs eye the Premier League.
fullText:
Swansea City and Wrexham will meet in the league for the 33rd time this Saturday evening.

Rarely, if ever, can there have been a more eagerly anticipated encounter between two clubs who are rivals, of sorts, despite being from opposite corners of Wales.

The fixture which matters most to Swansea fans is against Cardiff City, their neighbours in the south of the country.

For Wrexham, meanwhile, local squabbles with Chester and Shrewsbury Town have traditionally been the games which have come with the greatest significance.

But Swansea against Wrexham has a derby feel too, even though the cities are more than 100 miles apart.

And this particular meeting comes with increased stakes because both clubs have eyes on the Premier League.

Wrexham ended last season as top dogs in Wales, with Phil Parkinson's side finishing seventh in the Championship and Vitor Matos' Swansea seven points worse off in 11th.

It was the first time since 2000-01 - when they came 10th in what is now League One - that Wrexham had finished a campaign as the best-placed Welsh side in the English pyramid.

After three successive promotions, Wrexham, who beat Swansea at home in March after losing the reverse fixture last December, narrowly missed out on a play-off chance in May.

But their best-in-Wales status was another sign of the extraordinary progress they have made since Hollywood stars Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac took charge of the club in 2021.

Cardiff City's promotion from League One means that for only the third time, Wales' three heavyweight clubs are together in the second tier this season.

Given that the three teams have never competed together in the top flight - Swansea and Cardiff have met there in just one season, while Wrexham have not played at the highest level - a three-way Championship scrap is a big deal in Wales.

But to an extent the fight to be crowned the nation's leading team is a sideshow, with both Swansea and Wrexham chasing a greater prize.

Most observers would regard Cardiff as outsiders to feature in the promotion race next spring as they look to re-establish themselves at second-tier level.

But the picture is different for Swansea and Wrexham, who both showed considerable ambition in the transfer market for the second year in a row this summer as they look to compete with the Championship's top sides.

These are very early days in the season, but the signs from Swansea have been encouraging, with a tally of 10 points from four games putting them on top of the table.

They have conceded only one league goal so far - the best record in the EFL - while Matos' team produced some of Swansea's best football in years during Tuesday's win over Watford.

The Swans are in buoyant mood, while Wrexham should make the journey south with renewed confidence following their midweek triumph at Millwall.

The Red Dragons endured a concerning start to the season, with chances going begging in their draws with Cardiff and Watford before they were deservedly beaten at home by a Birmingham City team who were under pressure to deliver a result.

But the mood at the Racecourse has lightened significantly thanks to that emphatic victory over a Millwall side who are widely tipped to compete for promotion once more this season.

Another away success this weekend would make this a huge week for Parkinson and his players.

A home win, by contrast, would add to the feeling that Matos' new-look team could end Swansea's run of five successive mid-table Championship finishes by securing a place in the newly extended play-offs.

Swansea on the way to reviving style - Matos

Latest Wrexham news, analysis and fan views

The fact that Swansea against Wrexham has been selected for a Saturday evening live television slot says something about the interest in the game, which will be watched well beyond Wales' border.

There will be plenty looking on from the United States, for example, given the owners of the two clubs.

In the red corner are Reynolds and Mac, whose Welcome to Wrexham television series has turned what was a non-league football club into a global brand.

And in the white corner are Snoop Dogg, Luka Modric and Martha Stewart, all of whom have become co-owners at Swansea over the past 17 months.

The set-up at each club is different, with Reynolds and Mac the majority owners of Wrexham while Swansea's big names in the boardroom hold only minor stakes.

But the idea at Swansea, whose majority owners are American businessmen Brett Cravatt and Jason Cohen, is to "do a Wrexham" by raising their profile through the non-playing stars associated with the club.

Listen to the latest Swansea City interviews, news and discussion on BBC Sounds

Listen to the latest Wrexham interviews, news and discussion on BBC Sounds

The theory is that increased profile means increased income, which in turn allows more money to be spent on strengthening the team.

At this stage, it is difficult to judge what difference Snoop and Co have made.

But what is not in question is that for a second successive year, Swansea showed significant ambition in the transfer market.

Eight years after a golden period in their history ended with relegation from the Premier League, Swansea look like a club determined to have a serious go at getting back to the highest level.

For Wrexham, the goal is to join the elite for the first time, with their intent even more apparent based on the head-turning sums they have spent on transfers since promotion to the Championship in 2025.

We wait to discover whether either club has sufficient resources to mount a genuine push for the Premier League this season.

And while nothing will be decided in early September, there may be a few clues on offer this weekend.

title: Džeko relishing visit of "incredible" former teammate and Bayern coach Kompany
description: Ahead of Schalke's meeting with Bayern Munich this evening, Edin Dzeko was full of praise for his former teammate Vincent Kompany.“What Kompany has already achieved is incredible," said Dzeko, who s...
fullText:
Ahead of Schalke's meeting with Bayern Munich this evening, Edin Dzeko was full of praise for his former teammate Vincent Kompany.

"What Kompany has already achieved is incredible," said Dzeko, who shared a dressing room with the Bayern coach at Manchester City.

"He was always a captain and a leader, so none of this surprises me. We used to sit together at the very back of the bus.

"Kompany, Joleon Lescott, Aleksandar Kolarov and me. We listened to music and always had a lot of fun together.

"Meanwhile, Kompany would sit there looking at his laptop. 'What are you doing? What are you always studying?' we used to ask him.

"Then, when he got Burnley promoted as a manager, I texted him: 'Brate [brother], now I understand' [why you were on your laptop]'.

"I'm looking forward to seeing him. Hopefully, he won't take things quite so seriously on Saturday," the Bosnian striker joked.

The reigning Bundesliga champions travel to Gelsenkirchen to face second division winners Schalke at 18:30 CET this evening.

title: Geno Smith returns to the Jets eyeing a bold comeback after a brutal raiders collapse
description: Geno Smith returns to the Jets as their named starter after a brutal Raiders collapse. Inside the odds, the 2015 punch, and one more comeback bid.
fullText:
Geno Smith returns to the Jets eyeing a bold comeback after a brutal raiders collapse originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The New York Jets have handed their offense back to Geno Smith, and coach Aaron Glenn made the call fast, naming the 35-year-old his starter almost the moment a low-cost trade cleared.

The framing writes itself as a homecoming. Smith rejoins the club that took him in the second round in 2013, a draft slot he spent years treating as a snub. What the Jets are actually buying is a veteran fresh off a career-worst season, tasked with steadying a franchise that has not posted a winning record since he was hurt and pushed aside.

The math is harsh. Las Vegas went 3-14, secured the No. 1 pick, and moved on from Smith after his 17 interceptions topped the NFL, and he ranked 30th among 33 qualified passers in EPA per dropback.

He opens against the Tennessee Titans on Sept. 13 (1 p.m. ET, CBS) as the eighth player to start a season opener for the Jets in 11 years. His previous one came in 2014. No passer since the Super Bowl era began has waited longer, 12 years, between opening starts for a single franchise, per ESPN Research.

Smith sits 332 passing yards shy of moving past Zach Wilson for 10th on the Jets' all-time list, a marker that speaks to the position's churn more than to him. New York weighed him against Tua Tagovailoa before choosing the cheaper arm as a bridge to a stacked 2027 draft.

The reason the Jets trust a quarterback with this track record has less to do with his arm than with how the building responds to him. Wide receiver Adonai Mitchell calls him "the alpha in the room." Brandon Marshall, who lived with Smith before the 2015 season, put it plainly. "You can't push Geno over. That is needed in the locker room, especially today," he said.

That toughness got tested early. On Aug. 11, 2015, linebacker IK Enemkpali threw an uppercut over a $600 dispute, breaking Smith's jaw.

The QB1 job went to Ryan Fitzpatrick, and Smith's road since has wound through backup stops with the Giants, Chargers, and Seahawks before Pete Carroll installed him as Russell Wilson's successor in 2022. "Every single day he prepared like he was going to play the very next play," Carroll said.

There is a tactical wrinkle here. New York imported Raiders linemen Dylan Parham and Jordan Meredith and can point to the sacks Las Vegas surrendered, yet NFL Next Gen Stats flagged pressure on just five of his 17 picks. Rebuilding the pocket may not repair the reads. Frank Reich, the fifth man to call his plays in four seasons, inherits that puzzle.

Demario Davis, back with the Jets in 2026, sees a changed man. "You have to go through a certain amount of life to get that. You can't just buy it," he said. Smith is not looking backward. "It means that I've been in this league a while. And I intend to stay here."

title: No Brits left in US Open singles - but are there reasons to be positive?
description: There will be no British interest in the second week of another Grand Slam at the US Open - but is it all doom and gloom?
fullText:
For the fourth time in five majors, there will be no British interest in the second week when the US Open moves into the latter stages.

Underwhelming performances at this year's Australian Open, French Open and Wimbledon led to a series of inquests into what was going wrong.

But there is not quite the same sense of doom and gloom, despite everyone being wiped out after the second round in New York.

"Do I think there could be an inquest? I always think there's things that British tennis could do better. So yes, definitely," said British women's number three Francesca Jones.

"Do I think it's something that's concerning? No, not at all.

"The level is getting better and everyone is dangerous on their day."

With the Grand Slam season now over for the singles players, BBC Sport analyses the positives and negatives in British tennis.

Arthur Fery's extraordinary run to the Wimbledon semi-finals is the clear highlight.

The 24-year-old was ranked 114th in the world and needed a wildcard to play at the All England Club, but took full advantage to produce a performance which nobody could have predicted.

Fery was the only player to reach the second week at a Slam this year and has been heralded by British tennis bosses as proof their talent development pathway is working.

Nine Britons competing in the US Open main-draw singles - the most since 1981- is also highlighted as a sign of recent improvement.

That figure does not include 2021 US Open champion Emma Raducanu and Jack Draper, who both missed out with long-term injuries.

"We obviously want more and more competitors in the second week of Slams - just like the British public," said LTA chief executive Scott Lloyd.

"But the fact we've had four different British players make Grand Slam semi-finals since 2021 - you have to go back 30 years before Andy Murray to have four - shows there is no question that the direction of travel has improved.

"We've just got to keep driving for more - and that's what we're trying to do day in and day out."

Five British men are set to feature in the world top 100 after the US Open, with Fery, Cameron Norrie, Jan Choinski, Toby Samuel and Jacob Fearnley representing the highest tally since February 2024.

On the women's side, there will be two players - Katie Boulter and Raducanu - in the top 100, although Jones and Harriet Dart moved back to the cusp after reaching the Flushing Meadows second round.

"We've sent 12 players to the world's top 100 over the past eight years and four of those have played Grand Slam semi-finals," said LTA performance director Michael Bourne.

"I'm not sure what other period in the modern era where we've had that level of productivity. Hopefully the number in the top 100 will rise over the next year."

Despite those figures, some will argue that Britain - with its rich tradition and spending power as a Grand Slam nation - is still punching well below its weight.

A glut of injuries for many British players over the past year has not helped the cause.

Former world number four Draper has barely played over the past year because of an arm injury, while Sonay Kartal - who cracked the top 50 last year - has also dropped outside of the top 100 following a long-term back issue.

Britain has fewer players inside the top 100 than the United States, Australia and France, who also benefit from the revenue generated by hosting Grand Slam tournaments.

It also trails nations such as Spain, Italy, the Czech Republic and Argentina, who are all heralded for their talent production.

But Britain cannot simply "pick up a plan" of what others are doing as every country has its own "tennis ecosystem", says Bourne.

Lloyd adds: "We're competing in one of the most internationally elite sports out there and the landscape is vastly different to 40 or 50 years ago in terms of the number of countries which have representation at the top.

"We're ambitious, we want to drive for more, but we honestly believe the indicators are positive. We're moving in the right direction and stronger than where we have been historically."

Encouraging more British children to pick up a racquet from an early age is crucial to developing the next generation of stars.

Draper, Raducanu and Fery - who entered the LTA system at a young age - provide the blueprint.

There are 4.3m juniors playing tennis annually with 1.9m playing every month, which Lloyd says are both all-time records.

But there is a concern that a lack of high-level coaching is stunting the development of many more promising talents.

Bourne admits the UK needs a "higher base" of coaches, adding that one of the LTA's key strategies is "spending time and effort" on developing them.

Chris Marshall, a senior performance coach with over 25 years' experience, fears many youngsters are being priced out of tennis because parents cannot afford quality coaching.

"To fund a 12-year-old at county level right now requires anywhere from £500 to £1,000 a month for coaching, travel, and tournament fees," Marshall, who founded the Young Champs programme to provide free and discounted coaching for children, told BBC Sport.

"It is a massive, stressful financial barrier that makes the sport a non-starter for the vast majority of British families.

"We can't sit around lamenting the lack of British interest in the second week when we are restricting the pipeline that feeds it."

title: What is behind Lane Kiffin's disappearance from social media?
description: The LSU head coach was an active user on various social media platforms until this summer.
fullText:
What is behind Lane Kiffin's disappearance from social media? originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

New LSU head coach Lane Kiffin has long solidified himself as college football's favorite villain. The first-year Tigers head coach is currently embroiled in an eligibility battle to play former NFL players Zxavian Harris and Dae'Quan Wright.

But several fans familiar with Kiffin's antics might be wondering, "what has he been saying on social media about this?" In year's past, Kiffin would have been expected to live-tweet the whole situation.

But as of the fall of 2026, Kiffin's social media have been very quiet.

BENDER: Eight reasons why we still love college football

Kiffin's social media presence has been part of his persona as one of college football's most loved and hated main characters. For over a decade, Kiffin has been known to troll his former school, Tennessee, and Vol fans on X, formerly known as Twitter.

The LSU head coach actively posted on social media throughout his coaching career. He did so while he was at Alabama, as head coach at Florida Atlantic, and throughout his time as Ole Miss' head coach from 2020 through last year.

For example he trolled Brian Kelly after his Ole Miss team beat LSU last season:

Lane Kiffin trolled Brian Kelly on social media after Ole Miss defeated LSU 👀 pic.twitter.com/qQy3ehzkRA

When the rumors began to swirl that he was going to leave Ole Miss for the LSU job, his social media posts were becoming so cryptic that we compiled an entire story tracking them all.

After he accepted the LSU job, the posts continued into the winter and spring. From posting about landing recruits, to just random photos of LSU's various football facilities, his posts seemed like a stream of consciousness:

Good nite ⁦@LSUfootball⁩ pic.twitter.com/gH0tiPp9Gt

But early in the summer, Kiffin's social media posts went silent. A couple months later at SEC Media Days in July, Coach Kiffin told reporters that his silence stemmed from a bet with his son Knox, who apparently didn't think he could stay off of it.

"Really, it just started with Knox, my son, was sitting there and he's like, 'You're on social media; I bet you couldn't get off,'" Kiffin said via a local LSU radio host Matt Moscona. "If you follow me, if you tell me I can't do something, that's really a good way to get me to do it."

"So I just got off of everything," he continued. "Got off of it. Don't even have the apps, so it's not even like I read it either… I just wanted to show him I could do it. It's been really interesting as I look back over my life and my journey, a lot of great things have come when I've subtracted things out of my life and I've eliminated them."

Lane Kiffin explains his absence from social media.#LSU@1045espn@LASportsDotNetpic.twitter.com/IjX47dKxHz

"My kids have learned that too. If they really want something, just say I can't do it, and I'm going to do it," Kiffin said later at the podium at SEC Media Days. And so I'm like, 'Oh, I bet I can.'And it really wasn't a plan. So I got off of all of it. Then it was still on there. I said, okay, I'm going to go to another level, and I just deleted the apps. Wasn't a long-term plan.

"It was really interesting to see as I went through it because Knox pushing me to do that, challenging me, allowed me to help other players, friends, coaches to say, man, you should try this sometime because once you remove something from your life, you start to realize how many other people are addicted to it or need it."

MORE: Week 1 picks against the spread for Top 25 games

Kiffin's social media posts went silent around mid-May, but he posted what appeared to be a signal that it would be his last on June 18. He posted a Michael Jordan ad, which read that it was "time to go ghost:"

5/11/26 pic.twitter.com/dPABjcSAxg

In his explanation about going off social media at SEC Media Days, he actually made some good arguments about the effects of social media in general.

"Because now social media does what?" Kiffin added. "You sit there all day long, and you start to compare your job. You start to compare the city you live in. You start to compare your vacation, your kids, your clothes, your car, your significant other. When you don't see that all day, you're free of that comparison."

MORE:Ranking college football's new head coaches from Lane Kiffin to James Franklin

It appears that Kiffin will remain off social media for now, with the exception of posting advertisements that he is featured in. His first post since the hiatus was one of his Dr. Pepper college football ads:

#ad Nothing beats hitting the open road. Just me, my @DrPepper and a straight shot to Fansville. Watch here: https://t.co/W3aTfUKIPo

He also posted an ad via Door Dash

You don't have to fake being a player. The fans are getting rewarded this season 🔥

Order DoorDash on game days and get rewarded with weekly deals, discounts, and giveaways. #DoorDashPartner⁰
NO PURCHASE NECESSARY. Ends: 11:59 PM local time on 11/28/26. Open to 50 U.S./D.C.,…

For now, it appears that Kiffin's social media posts will remain quiet for most of the 2026 season.

title: Chelsea star says they are keen not to concede goals against Arsenal
description: Chelsea star Jorrel Hato is confident that the Blues can get a result when they face Arsenal in the Premier League this weekend, although the defender would love to see his team stop conceding as many...
fullText:
Chelsea star Jorrel Hato is confident that the Blues can get a result when they face Arsenal in the Premier League this weekend, although the defender would love to see his team stop conceding as many goals as they have done so far.

The Blues have opened their season with back-to-back wins and will face the Gunners knowing that scoring goals is unlikely to be a major problem. Chelsea have shown enough quality in attack to suggest they can trouble Arsenal during the match.

However, their defending has not yet reached the same level, with Chelsea conceding five goals in their opening two league matches. That means it is almost certain that Arsenal will also create chances and could score one or more goals against the Blues.

Keeping clean sheets alone does not win matches because teams must score goals to secure victories. However, preventing opponents from scoring can still be one of the key reasons why a team succeeds over the course of a season.

Arsenal are masters at keeping clean sheets, and Chelsea cannot assume that their meeting with the Gunners will turn into an open game in which both teams regularly find the net. The Blues could make a huge mistake if they expect Arsenal to allow them too many opportunities.

The Gunners have shown that they can shut teams out when they defend well, meaning Chelsea will need to be more disciplined at the back while still maintaining the attacking threat that has helped them win their first two league matches.

(Photo by Shaun Botterill/Getty Images)

Hato was speaking ahead of the match and explained that Chelsea are already looking to improve defensively. He also believes their attacking strength gives them confidence going into the challenge against Arsenal.

He said via Chelsea's official website:

'I can't see the future, but we try to improve to not concede three goals, but we know we are very dangerous up front, that we will score goals.

'I think against Arsenal is a good test, but I think it was against Fulham and Brighton as well. They are both great teams and we won those games, so we are looking forward to the next one now.'

Chelsea will now hope their defensive improvement can match their attacking confidence when they meet the Gunners.

title: How Yorkshire shaped the Brownlee era
description: A Jonny Brownlee retires, former coaches and teachers recall his and brother Alistair's impact.
fullText:
"I've had an incredible career. It's been nearly 30 years long and I've won more than I ever thought I'd ever achieve. It's time to move on because I wouldn't be doing myself justice by doing it half-heartedly."

Those were the words of triathlete Jonny Brownlee, who announced his retirement from professional sport on Friday, aged 36.

Now the Olympian is taking a step back from the starting line, former coaches, teachers and those inspired by his success have spoken about his legacy.

The younger Brownlee brother is a six-time world champion, and won gold, silver and bronze medals from the Olympic Games.

He and older brother Alistair, who twice won Olympic triathlon gold, grew up in the Leeds suburb of Horsforth, and both still live locally.

They were members of several sports clubs as children, including Bingley Harriers, and still have strong relationships with those they met there.

Their impact on triathlon, both locally, and beyond, can still be felt today, according to swimming teacher and the pair's former coach Coz Tantrum.

"They've got Yorkshire heart and they've got Yorkshire grit," she said.

Tantrum coached Jonny and Alistair from the ages of 11 and 13 respectively, when they joined the City of Bradford swimming club. Their early lessons in the pool were at Aireborough Leisure Centre in Guiseley.

Even from a young age, the brothers were committed to all three disciplines of the triathlon, Tantrum explained, although Jonny was the more "relaxed" of the pair.

"I'd finish the session and they'd literally sprint out of the pool and into the changing rooms.

"You'd see them outside handing the kit off to their parents and off they'd go, and they'd be running home or biking home."

Tantrum continued to coach the brothers until December last year, and witnessed first-hand their many successes and how they pushed each other, and the sport, on.

"They've got a massive amount of loyalty towards each other," she said.

For her, this was encapsulated when, in 2016, Alistair helped an exhausted Jonny over the line at the Triathlon World Series in Mexico.

"I think that's the moment when they became more than the triathlon brand.

"They transcended the triathlon, they transcended the sport, and there's not many people that can say they do that."

In the corner of Tantrum's swimming academy, she has a cabinet of Brownlee memorabilia to inspire others.

"If kids are getting into triathlon, everybody talks about them," she said.

"They have completely transformed triathlon. It's not just the legacy that they've left for Yorkshire, it's the legacy that they left for Great Britain."

PE teacher Matt Wilde taught all three Brownlee brothers at Bradford Grammar School - the youngest, Ed, is now a vet. Jonny also played team sports there, including rugby and cricket.

They were "incredibly intelligent, focused and ambitious" in their academic studies and sporting pursuits, he recalled.

"Bradford Grammar School is incredibly proud. They have inspired and still continue to inspire the pupils here."

Teaching alongside colleagues Tony Kingham, who ran the school running club, and Michael McCartney, Wilde said he felt "very fortunate" to play a small part in their lives.

The Old Bradfordians often return to their former school, to support the mini-triathlon event it holds annually, in association with the Brownlee Foundation.

The charity works with educational centres and other partners to introduce children to active lifestyles through all three triathlon sports.

Wilde added that although the pair are "superstars" it still felt "very normal" to see them back on school grounds.

"They are history makers but they're just well-grounded, normal individuals who have achieved such a huge amount in the world of triathlon," he said.

There are others in the region that had more fleeting, yet just as memorable, encounters with the Brownlees.

Back in 2012, organisers at York Parkrun were astonished to see Jonny - on the cusp of his first Olympic medal - turn up to take part in the weekly 5km event.

One of the volunteers that day said the young athlete turned up with "no fuss, no entourage".

"The story goes that he had been up studying all night and decided to come out and stretch his legs at York Parkrun," they said.

The course record in 2012 was 15 minutes and 57 seconds which Jonny comfortably bested with 14:43. It stood until 2017.

The volunteer added that "as a relatively new Parkrun and being in the lead-up to the 2012 Olympics, his visit did give us a lot of pride".

For their entire careers, the brothers used training facilities at the University of Leeds, where Jonny also studied history.

Even their kit requirements were met locally, as they were regular customers at triathlon specialists Triangle in Guiseley.

The late owner Adam Nevins, who died in a motorcycle accident in 2023, gave them advice on equipment when they were first entering races as children.

The Brownlee Centre, a collaboration between the university and Leeds Beckett, is the first purpose-built triathlon training centre in the UK.

Rhys Davey, head of triathlon at the centre, spent many years training alongside the brothers, having first met them at university.

He described their commitment to training as "immense" from the very beginning.

"Not only are buildings named after them and a cycle track, but they really have inspired a generation of young people to do triathlon.

"They are a huge part of the reason [the centre] has grown to where it is today."

Pete Mackreth, dean of Carnegie School of Sport at Leeds Beckett, said the university congratulated Jonny "on an incredible career full of medals and memorable moments".

After the retirement of Alistair in 2024, Jonny's decision brings the curtain down on the Brownlee era of triathlon and their contribution to the sport entering the mainstream.

Mackreth added: "He's contributed to securing an incredible legacy for triathlon in the UK and in Leeds, helping to make the city a global centre of excellence in the sport," he said.

"I am sure Jonny will continue his long relationship with Leeds Beckett, and hope he remains a regular on campus whatever he decides to do next."

title: Has there been a changing of guard for London sides in the WSL?
description: With the Women's Super League season starting up, are Arsenal in a better position than Chelsea to challenge for the title?
fullText:
Last season, Arsenal finished above Chelsea in the Women's Super League for the first time in seven years.

The last occasion was in 2018-19, the most recent title for the Gunners.

In between, Chelsea finished top of the pile for six straight seasons.

In 2025-26, while both trailed in the wake of eventual champions Manchester City, Arsenal leapfrogged their London rivals to finish second.

They also knocked the Blues out of the Women's Champions League in the quarter-finals.

So did those results signal a changing of the guard in the capital?

And what about London City Lionesses, who opened the WSL season with victory over Manchester United on Friday and now boast Spain superstar Alexia Putellas in their ranks?

This summer, both Arsenal and Chelsea have experienced turnover in their squads.

The Gunners lost stalwarts Beth Mead and Katie McCabe among others but have freshened their team with England midfielder Georgia Stanway, Spain World Cup winner Ona Batlle and Switzerland captain Geraldine Reuteler among a glut of exciting signings.

At Stamford Bridge, Chelsea snapped up McCabe on a free transfer and splashed cash on Manchester United's Melvine Malard but can no longer call on Sam Kerr and Millie Bright, two defining players from their era of dominance.

With their latest quest for silverware getting started this weekend, it was Arsenal boss Renee Slegers who struck a more confident tone about her expectations for the season.

"We've been open about it - the WSL title is something we're going after," said Slegers, before her side open the season at Brighton on Sunday. "It's something where we really have our mind set.

"Of course there's a big belief in what we are doing, the quality that we possess and the different tools we have to use. There's a real hunger."

Sunday's game offers Arsenal an early return to Broadfield Stadium in Crawley, where their bid to chase down Manchester City last season was ended by a 1-1 draw against Brighton in May.

A number of similar results cost Arsenal, particularly at the beginning of the year, and Slegers is determined to avoid lightning striking twice.

"We've spoken about it with the staff, the captains, the player group," she said. "Everyone is aware of it. We know the hurdles we had last year - and that's what we're working towards.

"The quality of players that we have here, there's so many things that we can bring to a game now. I'm really happy about it."

And is this her strongest squad at Arsenal?

At Chelsea, manager Sonia Bompastor was less bullish about her side's chances of regaining the WSL title.

"I'm trying to be as honest as possible. Chelsea is in a transitional phase," Bompastor said. "We are rebuilding, regenerating the squad.

"As much as I know my job is to win many games and to win trophies and I'm desperate for that - but it also takes time for the squad to gel together."

"The DNA for Chelsea is to win and we want to make sure we go as far as possible in every competition."

Saturday, 5 September, 12:30 BST

Chelsea open the season against Aston Villa on Saturday lunchtime, live on BBC One, and have been installed as favourites by Opta's supercomputer, which gives the Blues a 39.9% chance, external of winning the league.

Not that Bompastor is paying any attention.

"I remember sitting here last season and someone told me the same," she said. "Our percentage was higher than this season! I'm not too focused on what numbers and what is coming from AI or computers."

She believes that this season will be the toughest yet and, while acknowledging the significant threat from champions Manchester City, she says challengers will come from all directions.

"The beauty in this league is that many clubs are in a position to win the title," Bompastor said. "It was already the most competitive league in the world and it's becoming stronger every season.

"Every game is so difficult but that's good. I'm excited for it."

One of those could be London City, who after finishing sixth in their maiden WSL season have spent big this summer.

Their goal is likely to be challenging the established elite in the WSL, although ambitious owner Michelle Kang will not settle for that.

She has previously told BBC Sport that London City "have an aspiration to be at the top of the game" and starting the season with a convincing performance against Manchester United lends credence to that plan.

title: Taylor v Pili - Irish icon's farewell fight predictions
description: Figures from the boxing world give their predictions for Katie Taylor's farewell fight against Flora Pili in Dublin on Saturday. .
fullText:
Katie Taylor brings the curtain down on a remarkable career on Saturday when she faces unbeaten Flora Pili in front of 80,000 fans at Croke Park in Dublin.

Taylor is an Olympic gold medallist and two-weight undisputed champion who has won 25 of her 26 professional fights, with six victories by stoppage.

The 40-year-old has long dreamed of fighting at Croke Park and will finally get her wish in the final bout of her career.

French challenger Pili, 29, is undefeated in 12 professional contests, with two stoppage wins. She is former European champion, but has never faced anyone with Taylor's pedigree or experience.

Victory in the light-welterweight contest would provide a fairytale ending for one of Ireland's greatest sporting careers and see Taylor become an undisputed champion for a third time.

Can Taylor produce one final vintage performance on the biggest night of her career?

Or will the younger, unbeaten Pili spoil the occasion and pull off a mammoth upset?

BBC Sport spoke to figures from the boxing world to get their predictions for Saturday's fight.

"Saturday is the perfect tribute to probably the greatest female boxer that has ever lived in Katie Taylor. Flora Pili has the perfect style that will make Katie Taylor look great.

"It'll be a brilliant night and it will be capped off with a fantastic performance from Katie Taylor."

"100% Katie Taylor wins. It will be a night where she captures the hearts of not just Ireland but so many nations. She is the purest of souls and that is so much more of boxing. I pray that when she leaves that ring she knows what she has done for the people who will come through in boxing."

"I think we see Katie rolling back the years and one more Katie Taylor performance. I wouldn't be surprised if we saw a late stoppage and capped an unbelievable career. She will get a homecoming fit for a queen.

"I'm very jealous I'm not there but I'm not ruling out getting a flight there and doing an all-nighter and getting the 6am flight back home."

"Katie Taylor is going to have an amazing performance and this is what she's wanted at Croke Park. Taylor will give it her all during her last rodeo and will put on an amazing performance to get the win."

"I've watched bits of Pili and she looks OK, but Katie is on a different level and should win, will win. It will be the icing on the cake for Katie to end a career that we may never see again from a fighter from these shores.

"It's a little harder for the women to get stoppages with the two-minute rounds, but I feel Katie may well find a finish in the later rounds."

Coverage on Radio 5 Sports Extra from 19:00 BST, then 5 Live from 22:00. Ringwalks for main event expected between 22:00 and 22:30.

"It's going to be a very special evening and I think Katie wins by mid-to-late stoppage. She's always been one to rise to the occasion and with this being her swansong, I think she will put on an unbelievable performance on an unbelievable night.

"There will be plenty of tears shed in Croke Park and I can't wait to witness the greatest ever athlete our country has produced, male or female, go out in style."

"It will be a great send off for the great Katie Taylor. I don't think Katie will have too much trouble with Flora Pili, who is decent but I think she will be overawed with the pressure and the combination punches.

"Katie rarely gets a stoppage but I think she will this time. It's a clear win and she can sail off into the sunset as the greatest female boxer there has ever been."

"Katie Taylor has her dream opportunity as she closes her unprecedented career. She has been the pioneer, standout female fighter and jewell in the Emerald Isle.

"Flora Pili will do her very best but I think Katie will come through to win, claim the undisputed title and bow out in style."

"Boxing always has this way of throwing a curve ball, there's always a banana skin somewhere and this might be it.

"Katie Taylor hasn't fought for nearly a year-and-a-half when she had the trilogy with Amanda Serrano. She's 40-years-old, there's a lot of wear and tear and mileage on her. The same can't be said for Pili. She's fought a few levels down but she's unbeaten and will come with confidence.

"I think Katie will get it done but don't think it will be without problems, so Taylor to get it done on a close decision."
