title: MUST SEE: USC’s 6-foot-8 giant Elijah Vaikona goes viral during Fresno State game
description: USC offensive lineman Elijah Vaikona became an immediate viral attraction after viewers saw the 6-foot-8 giant during Friday night’s game.
fullText:
MUST SEE: USC's 6-foot-8 giant Elijah Vaikona goes viral during Fresno State game originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

There are big offensive linemen, and then there is USC tackle Elijah Vaikona. The Trojans' massive redshirt freshman became an instant social media attraction during Friday night's game against Fresno State after the television broadcast offered another look at his remarkable frame.

Yahoo Sports shared the clip with a simple observation that captured what nearly everyone watching was thinking.

"USC's Elijah Vaikona is a massive human being," Yahoo Sports wrote.

That almost feels like an understatement.

Vaikona is listed at 6-foot-8 and 360 pounds on USC's updated roster, although he previously weighed as much as 385 pounds. Even while surrounded by other Division I football players, the young offensive tackle is nearly impossible to miss.

The visual quickly became one of the most memorable moments from moments from USC's second game of the 2026 season. Vaikona is not simply a novelty, either. He is a developing prospect who could eventually become an important piece of Lincoln Riley's offensive line.

Vaikona joined USC as a three-star member of its 2025 recruiting class after playing at Santa Margarita Catholic High School in California. He selected the Trojans over programs including UCLA and Washington. His extraordinary size naturally became the first thing recruiting analysts noticed.

USC's Elijah Vaikona is a massive human being 😲 pic.twitter.com/h9YzNr1doQ

"One of the largest humans we've ever seen on a football field," 247Sports national recruiting analyst Greg Biggins wrote while evaluating Vaikona.

Vaikona appeared in four games during his first season at USC. The Trojans also used him for nine snaps in the Alamo Bowl, including specialized packages designed to take advantage of his enormous frame.

He entered the 2026 season as part of a deep offensive tackle group. USC returned starters Elijah Paige and Justin Tauanuu while adding talented young linemen Aaron Dunn and Keenyi Pepe to the competition. That depth should allow the Trojans to remain patient with Vaikona as he develops his technique and improves his movement. There are physical traits that cannot be taught, however, and Vaikona already possesses those in abundance.

MORE: Deion Sanders fires back at Colorado critics after stunning Georgia Tech upset

Vaikona's appearance attracted attention Friday, but the long-term intrigue comes from what USC could eventually do with him. At 6-foot-8, he has the length to create problems for edge rushers before they can reach his body. His weight gives him the potential to overwhelm defenders in the running game and make him especially valuable in short-yardage situations.

The former basketball player still must prove he has the agility and consistency to handle Big Ten pass rushers. If his technique catches up with his size, USC could have an unusually imposing tackle on its hands.

For one night, though, Vaikona did not need to throw a block to get college football fans talking.

He only needed to appear on camera.

title: Giants' Cam Skattebo Reveals Conversation With John Harbaugh About Role
description: New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo has spoken with head coach John Harbaugh about his role on the team for the 2026 season.
fullText:
New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo is poised to have a large role in his second season in the league. Skattebo had a quality rookie year before going down with a season-ending ankle injury.

He will now be the lead running back for the Giants in the 2026 season, and it appears Harbaugh is preparing him for a large role in the offense.

"When he walks up to me and tells me, 'Are you ready for 20-plus carries a game?' I think I'm in a pretty good spot," Skattebo said.

Skattebo could have a breakout season if he gets 20-plus touches a game for New York's offense. In his rookie season, he rushed for 410 yards and five touchdowns, along with 24 receptions for 207 yards and two touchdowns in eight games.

He proved to be an efficient rusher who can also be impactful in the receiving game.

With Skattebo healthy, he will play a huge role in the Giants' offense alongside the other young talent of quarterback Jaxson Dart and wide receiver Malik Nabers.

Dart is also entering his second season in the league, after completing 63.7 percent of his passes for 2,272 yards, 15 touchdowns, and five interceptions. The 23-year-old was also effective in the run game, rushing for 487 yards and nine touchdowns on 86 attempts.

When Dart and Skattebo were on the field together, it gave a glimpse into what New York's offense could look like at its best. They will now be joined by Nabers, who is returning from a torn ACL, which he suffered in Week 4 of the 2025 season.

Nabers had an incredible rookie season, hauling in 109 receptions for 1,204 yards and seven touchdowns in 2024. He was off to a solid start in 2025, with 18 receptions for 271 yards and two touchdowns before suffering the season-ending injury.

With the young offensive pieces in place and a new head coach in Harbaugh, the Giants have a lot of hope ahead of the 2026 season. Skattebo will be a big part of the offense and build upon the solid rookie season he put together.

title: Pro Football Hall of Fame overhauls voting process
description: Starting with next year's voting, things are changing for the Pro Football Hall of Fame. See what is different now.
fullText:
The Pro Football Hall of Fame has decided to make some changes. In part, it is because legendary New England Patriots head coach Bill Belichick somehow didn't make it in his first year of eligibility.

The number of Hall of Fame voters is being reduced from 50 to 28, and there will no longer be at least one voter from each NFL market.

There will now be 27 at-large selectors and onw PFWA representative.

There will no longer be a "senior" category, so players simply remain eligible as part of the regular vote, even after 25 years.

Rather than a candidate list of 15 modern-era players, three senior candidates, one coach and one contributor, it will now be 13 players, one coach and one contributor, which the one coach and one contributor being determined by their sub-committees.

There will be no more carryover finalist candidates as previously there have been. Players who made the final seven will not be automatic finalists the next year.

As it takes appearing on 80% of ballots to be enshrined, it is expected that most years will have five or six enshrinees.

We will see how this impacts voting moving forward, and whether it will ultimately help or hurt candidates who have been waiting a while.

title: Tottenham’s Mikey Moore furnishes impressive Bundesliga debut for Cologne
description: Mikey Moore required only a few minutes of his Bundesliga debut to demonstrate why 1. FC Köln spent most of August attempting to secure his services from Tottenham Hotspur. The 19-year-old entered at...
fullText:
Mikey Moore required only a few minutes of his Bundesliga debut to demonstrate why 1. FC Köln spent most of August attempting to secure his services from Tottenham Hotspur. The 19-year-old entered at half-time of Friday night's 4-1 defeat away at VfB Stuttgart and immediately transformed a Cologne attack that had offered precious little during the opening 45 minutes.

René Wagner's side had been thoroughly outplayed before the break. Wagner responded with two changes. Ellyes Skhiri replaced Paul Okon-Engstler in midfield while Moore came on for Jan Thielmann and moved into a central attacking position behind Ragnar Ache.

The impact was immediate. Moore attacked Finn Jeltsch virtually straight from the restart and earned Köln a corner. Skhiri nearly equalized from the resulting sequence, forcing Fabian Bredlow into an excellent close-range save.

Moore then began finding exactly the spaces Stuttgart had largely denied Cologne before the interval.

In the 53rd minute, the Tottenham loanee broke the line, escaped Grischa Prömel with an intelligent turn and forced Bredlow into another strong save with his foot. Three minutes later, Moore was involved again as Cologne countered through Ache. The striker released Moore on the right, with Bredlow once more denying the teenager before Josha Vagnoman blocked Ache's follow-up.

Cologne had suddenly gone from struggling to enter dangerous areas to creating clear chances in rapid succession.

The final 4-1 scoreline therefore did little justice to Moore's individual contribution. Over only 45 minutes, the England youth international registered two shots and created two shooting opportunities for teammates. His work produced 0.72 expected assists, an unusually high figure for a player who spent only half the match on the pitch.

Moore completed 92 percent of his 13 passes, attempted two dribbles and recorded 11 sprints while covering 5.83 kilometers.

His influence remained visible even after Stuttgart restored control. Moore helped create Cologne's lone goal in the 81st minute. Reigan Heskey released him into space before Moore drove a low ball across the six-yard box toward Marius Bülter. Ramon Hendriks supplied the final touch while attempting to intervene, meaning the strike was officially recorded as a Stuttgart own goal rather than a Moore assist.

Friday's appearance came only days after Cologne finally completed a transfer they had pursued for almost an entire month. An agreement was reached last month, but Tottenham temporarily delayed final approval as head coach Roberto De Zerbi considered keeping the youngster in North London.

Cologne eventually got their man.

The 19-year-old officially joined Wagner's squad on a season-long loan without a purchase option. Moore already possesses an unusual amount of senior experience for his age. His tactical profile also appears particularly well suited to Wagner's plans. Against Stuttgart, Moore's first Bundesliga minutes came centrally. His performance suggested that role may provide Köln with another highly valuable attacking option.

Wagner specifically praised both half-time substitutes when reflecting on Cologne's improved second-half performance.

"At halftime, we brought on two players in Mike and Flaco [Skhiri] that were important to us," Wagner responded when asked to comment on Moore and his fellow half-time substitute Ellyes Skhiri. "We witnessed how dangerous Mike can be between the lines and how he can turn. He can create chances. He can get into the box. He's a player who can make a difference for us. One saw that with Flaco too, the way he organized the game."

title: Mariners’ Matt Brash suffers setback in injury rehab, done for the year
description: Mariners injury updates: Matt Brash, Brendan Donovan, Emerson Hancock
fullText:
A couple of injured Mariners have had setbacks in their progression as they attempt to return to play: reliever Matt Brash has been shut down from throwing temporarily, while infielder Brendan Donovan remains in the concussion protocol.

UPDATE: Mariners GM Justin Hollander announced to the media on Friday that the results of an MRI taken on Thursday showed inflammation in his injured lat. Brash felt tightness in his lat after throwing his most recent bullpen in Boston, so the team shut him down from throwing for the time being while he got imaging done. Unfortunately, that imaging revealed the inflammation, and the team has shut him down from throwing for the next eight weeks in order to clear the inflammation. He'll obviously miss the rest of the season, but the hope is that he can start his off-season throwing program sometime in early November provided the inflammation calms.

According to GM Justin Hollander, this was been a recurring pattern for Brash as he attempted to clear the hurdle of bullpens off a mound before graduating to throwing to live hitters and then to a rehab assignment.

"This has been a recurring theme with this specific injury," said Hollander. "He feels good when he's throwing on flat ground, but in the pens, it's continued to tighten up on him as he finishes the bullpen and gets into the recovery phase."

"He's bounced back reasonably. Not as much as we would have hoped, which is why we've been in the same holding pattern where he's throwing bullpens but hasn't progressed to live BPs or game action because this has been a pattern over the last 10 days – two weeks, where he feels really good in between, he feels really good throwing on flat, he feels fine in the bullpen, then after the pen, it starts to tighten up a little bit. And until we can get through that, there's just no reason to push him out there and cause more injury or have a recurrence of the same injury."

Even with a perfect scan, it seemed very unlikely that Brash would have been able to rejoin the team before the end of the regular season. But it's still disappointing news, and another tile in the sad mosaic of injury and ineffectiveness that has been the 2026 Mariners season.

Brash isn't the only Mariner who has struggled to clear an injury benchmark. Infielder Brendan Donovan remains in the concussion protocol. The benchmark he's not able to clear yet is being able to complete his pregame work without feeling symptoms of his concussion – he'll get to the end of his pregame routine and feel effects such as nausea, fatigue, and/or dizziness. Hollander called Donovan's progress "incremental" and "slow" and said all the team can do is continue to see if he can clear that benchmark before a return to play can be considered, at which point the team will determine whether to send him back to Tacoma for a couple of rehab games or activate him straight to the big-league team.

"Some days are better than others," said Hollander. "The last few days, he has felt symptomatic towards all of thsoe pregames…it's just not okay if we run him out there when he's feeling those things until he can get all the way through them and feel 100%."

Hollander also provided an update on Emerson Hancock, who is currently on the IL with a groin strain. Hancock will throw on Sunday, either from a mound or flat ground, at which point the team will have more information about how he's feeling and decisions will be made about how to proceed.

There's better news for another injured Mariners reliever: reliever Cole Wilcox will throw off a mound this weekend, and the hope is he'll be able to throw a couple of bullpens with the goal of getting in some rehab games in Tacoma before the Triple-A season ends, and then ideally be available for the Mariners after that.

Hollander also updated Emerson Hancock's status on Friday, saying he had a follow-up MRI that was "encouraging." He's scheduled to throw on Sunday, which will hopefully provide clarity about his availability moving forward.

One final note: newly-acquired reliever Hoby Milner is away from the team attending to a family emergency. RHP Troy Taylor is up from Tacoma in his place.

title: Mauricio Dubón, Chris Sale help Braves win series opener at Phillies
description: A tone-setter to begin a crucial series.
fullText:
Mauricio Dubón continues to be a lethal and versatile weapon for the Atlanta Braves.

Making a fairly rare start in center field for Friday's series opener at the Philadelphia Phillies as the Braves elected to sit Michael Harris II against a left-handed starter, Dubón paid off that decision with a leaping catch in the outfield and, more importantly, an insurance homer late in Atlanta's 5-2 win over the Phillies.

With the Braves clinging to a 3-2 lead after escaping a few jams where the Phillies threatened to tie the game or take the lead, Dubón followed Mike Yastrzemski's one-out walk with a 390-foot two-run blast to left for his 11th homer of the season.

Dubón finished the night with two hits, two runs and two RBIs.

The Braves (84-57) didn't end up needing the insurance as a rested bullpen didn't allow a single baserunner over the final three innings after Chris Sale's strong start. But it still allowed for some breathing room which made for a less stressful conclusion

The win pushed the Braves' record against the Phillies to 6-1 and their NL East lead to five games. It also means that if Atlanta wins one of its final six games against Philadelphia, it will hold the head-to-head tiebreaker should the teams end up tied in the standings.

The Braves came up empty in the first inning despite Ronald Acuña Jr.'s first-pitch double to right-center to lead off the game.

But Atlanta would not be denied in the second inning. After Lane Thomas walked and Dubón singled to begin the inning, the bottom of the order came through with some situational hitting. Austin Riley opened the scoring with an RBI single to right, and Ha-Seong Kim followed with an RBI groundout to make it 2-0.

Acuña then came through for the second time in as many innings, this time with a two-out RBI single to score Riley and extend the Atlanta lead to 3-0.

Unfortunately for the Braves, that proved to be all they could manage against Phillies ace Cristopher Sánchez. Starting with the final out of the second inning, he faced 13 of the final 16 batters he faced, giving up three runs on five hits over six innings with five strikeouts and three walks.

Still, Sánchez took his second loss to the Braves in as many starts this season, accounting for 40% of his five losses this campaign.

The Phillies gradually chipped into that deficit behind a pair of moments from Alec Bohm, who delivered an RBI double in the second inning and a wall-scraper of a solo homer in the fourth inning — the first homer Sale had allowed since July 4.

Sale, though, ensured Atlanta would remain ahead when he exited the game after six innings thanks to some impressive resolve.

The Phillies put two runners in scoring position with two outs in the fifth, but Sale got Bryce Harper to pop out to third base to end the threat.

Philadelphia again put the tying run in scoring position with a leadoff double from Luis Arráez in the sixth, but Sale retired the next three batters, the last two by strikeout, to end his outing.

Sale gave up two runs on six hits, striking out seven and walking one.

Acuña added a third hit, an infield single, in the seventh inning. He now has three three-hit games in his last seven appearances after he had none in his first 81 games of the season.

Paired with the Dubón homer, Didier Fuentes and Raisel Iglesias ensured there would be no late-inning drama. Fuentes retired all six batters he faced over the seventh and eighth innings on 21 pitches (18 strikes). Iglesias worked a 1-2-3 ninth with a pair of strikeouts to register his 30th save of the season.

A win in the opener takes some of the pressure off for the Braves. They now need to win just one of the next three games to ensure a split with the Phillies in this road four-game set and keep their division lead at least as large as it was entering the weekend.

They'll look to secure that Saturday night with Martín Pérez (8-8, 3.05 ERA) facing off against Philadelphia's Zack Wheeler (11-5, 3.31).

title: LA Clippers Get Brutal Nikola Jokic Reality Despite Nuggets’ Slow Summer
description: Once Nikola Jokic rejected extension talks this summer, it just gave other NBA teams hope that the Denver Nuggets superstar might pack up and leave Colorado as early as next season. Apparently, the Los Angeles Clippers were one of the teams quietly hoping for it. According to the NBA analyst Zach Lowe, you can count […] The post LA Clippers Get Brutal Nikola Jokic Reality Despite Nuggets’ Slow Summer appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Once Nikola Jokic rejected extension talks this summer, it just gave other NBA teams hope that the Denver Nuggets superstar might pack up and leave Colorado as early as next season.

Apparently, the Los Angeles Clippers were one of the teams quietly hoping for it.

According to the NBA analyst Zach Lowe, you can count LA out of any future Jokic sweepstakes, as their punishment from the league places them in an extremely difficult spot.

"The Clippers are somewhere beyond f*****," Lowe said on a recent episode of his podcast.

"For an organization that has struggled for relevancy, basically its entire existence, this is pretty close to a death knell for a decade, a half decade. We don't even know. They're already rebuilding. A front office executive from another team, not the Clippers, not the Denver Nuggets, who are about to come up, say, 'Hey, the Clippers are kind of quietly positioning themselves in case Jokic actually wants to leave Denver with lots of cap space and LA and all that.' Forget that. This team is dead. Those superstars aren't going there when they're out five first-round picks, and they can't put together real trades and all that."

After over one year of being investigated for salary cap circumvention, the Clippers were indeed found to be in the wrong. The NBA surely didn't hold back with the punishment.

Jokic's interest outside of Denver is unknown. Based on what he has said publicly, the veteran center still claims he wants to be with the Nuggets for the long haul. Even if that's not one-hundred percent true, he will almost certainly overlook the Clippers if the veteran center has a chance of heart about Denver.

The Clippers lost five future first-round picks.

The team was hit with a $30 million fine, while the owner Steve Ballmer was hit with a one-year suspension. The team's president of business operations is also suspended for one year, while the president of basketball operations is suspended for six months.

While the NBA star Kawhi Leonard landed a punishment of his own, he is still expected to part ways with the organization. The Toronto Raptors are expected to soon finalize the deal to acquire the veteran forward.

title: LeBron James-Kobe Bryant 1-of-1 autographed jersey patch card goes to auction after sitting in private collection for nearly 20 years
description: A Kobe-Michael Jordan card from the same 2007-08 Upper Deck set sold for a record $12.93 million in August 2025
fullText:
A one-of-one sports card featuring autographs from Kobe Bryant and LeBron James in addition to game-worn NBA logo jersey patches from the NBA legends will sell at a public auction held by trading card marketplace Alt this month.

"This card was in a private collection for a couple of decades and no one knew it was available," Alt senior account executive Brendan Kirbach told The Athletic's Benjamin Burrows. "It was just sitting raw in someone's collection."

The 2007-08 Upper Deck Exquisite Collection Dual Logoman card was held in a collection in ungraded condition for nearly 20 years before being sold to the current owner, who had the card graded by the Professional Sports Authenticator (PSA) grading service last month. The card was graded as an 8 (on a 1-10 scale), according to The Athletic.

BREAKING NEWS: The biggest card to hit auction is now live on Alt.

The one-of-one 2007 Kobe Bryant and LeBron James Exquisite Logoman Auto.

After sitting ungraded for nearly 20 years, this one-of-a-kind card was recently graded and received a PSA 8.

This once-in-a-lifetime… pic.twitter.com/EBgHRNnjWy

The Bryant-James card is from the same set as a one-of-one Bryant and Michael Jordan Dual Logoman card that sold for $12.93 million through Heritage Auctions a year ago. With that price, it became the most expensive sports card ever sold, going for more than twice what Heritage estimated.

(A Bryant-Jordan Dual Logoman card that wasn't autographed sold for $3.12 million through Heritage Auctions in December 2025.)

Could the Kobe-LeBron card surpass the record $12.93 million? Alt wouldn't put a pre-sale estimate on the card, but PSA told The Athletic that the item is among the most valuable cards that the service has graded this year.

Possibly adding to the value is the card being issued in 2007-08. Bryant won the only NBA MVP award of his career that season, as Men's Journal pointed out. And LeBron James won the only scoring title of his career, averaging 30 points per game.

The bidding for the Kobe-LeBron card opened on Friday and has already surpassed $2 million, according to Sports Collectors Daily. The auction will run through Sept. 24.

title: Celtics Trade Pitch Sends 3 Players, 2 Picks for New Jayson Tatum Co-Star
description: A Celtics trade pitch sends three players and two first-round picks for a new co-star to pair with Jayson Tatum. The post Celtics Trade Pitch Sends 3 Players, 2 Picks for New Jayson Tatum Co-Star appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Boston Celtics did not trade Jaylen Brown merely to get older.

Paul George was part of the return, but the real currency Boston acquired from Philadelphia was flexibility — both financial and in the form of future draft capital. If Brad Stevens eventually decides to cash some of that capital in for another long-term running mate for Jayson Tatum, Trey Murphy III should be near the top of the list.

Boston was already linked to Murphy earlier this summer as a potential alternative if its pursuit of Giannis Antetokounmpo fell short. That interest made sense then. It makes even more sense now that Brown is in Philadelphia and the Celtics have a clearer need for a second star-caliber wing beside Tatum.

Here is one aggressive framework that could get New Orleans' attention.

Pelicans receive: Payton Pritchard
Sam Hauser
Chris Cenac Jr.
Boston's 2030 first-round pick
Philadelphia's unprotected 2031 first-round pick

There is no indication the teams have discussed this exact package. It is a proposal built around what New Orleans has reportedly sought for Murphy and what Boston can realistically afford to move.

The Pelicans' asking price has been steep. They began around four first-round picks before lowering the price to at least three, Hoopshype's Michael Scotto previously reported, and there has been skepticism around the league over whether New Orleans truly intends to move him at all.

Boston's offer would effectively give the Pelicans three first-round-caliber assets: Cenac, the No. 27 pick in June, plus two actual firsts.

Murphy is not Brown, and Boston should not ask him to be.

At 26, the 6-foot-8 wing is entering his prime and coming off a season in which he averaged 21.5 points, 5.7 rebounds and 3.8 assists while shooting 37.9% from 3-point range.

Next to Tatum, Murphy would not need to dominate possessions. He can sprint into transition, punish tilted defenses as a catch-and-shoot threat, attack closeouts and defend either forward spot.

For a Celtics team that suddenly lacks a clear second offensive star, that kind of low-maintenance production would carry real value. Boston's current core still includes Tatum, Derrick White and George, but George is 36 and cannot reasonably be viewed as the long-term answer beside Tatum.

Boston's cap position makes the structure important.

The Celtics are roughly $10.3 million below the first apron and hard-capped there. Their payroll sits at about $198.7 million.

Pritchard makes $7.8 million, Hauser $10.8 million and Cenac about $3 million. Together, that is roughly $21.6 million going out.

Under the NBA's matching rules, Boston can take that salary back while remaining beneath its hard cap. The deal would raise the Celtics' payroll by a little more than $5 million, leaving them with a few million dollars of breathing room.

That matters because the entire rationale behind moving Brown was to escape the roster-building restrictions created by multiple massive contracts. Stevens said after the deal that future flexibility was central to Boston's thinking.

Murphy offers star-level upside without another $50 million salary.

The Brown deal also replenished Boston's draft chest.

The Celtics received a complicated 2028 first-round asset tied to Philadelphia and the Clippers, an unprotected 2031 Philadelphia first and two second-round picks. The 2031 first could become particularly valuable because Philadelphia's current contender is built around an aging core.

Boston also controls future firsts of its own, giving Stevens enough ammunition to chase a premium player without stripping the cupboard completely bare.

The price for Murphy would still hurt.

Pritchard is one of the NBA's better value guards. Hauser is a proven shooter. Cenac represents a young frontcourt prospect. And a 2031 unprotected Philadelphia first is exactly the kind of distant asset teams hesitate to surrender.

But the Celtics did not trade Brown to collect draft picks indefinitely.

At some point, those picks have to become players who can help Tatum win.

Murphy is young enough to grow with him and good enough to matter immediately. That is exactly the kind of bet Boston should be willing to make.

title: Los Angeles Dodgers Announce Concerning Shohei Ohtani Decision Before Nationals Series
description: The Los Angeles Dodgers secured a 3-2 victory over the St. Louis Cardinals on Thursday night to improve to 83-57 on the season. On Friday, they’ll begin a series at home against the Washington Nationals, and ahead of the matchup, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts made a fairly concerning decision regarding superstar Shohei Ohtani, who seems […] The post Los Angeles Dodgers Announce Concerning Shohei Ohtani Decision Before Nationals Series appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Dodgers secured a 3-2 victory over the St. Louis Cardinals on Thursday night to improve to 83-57 on the season.

On Friday, they'll begin a series at home against the Washington Nationals, and ahead of the matchup, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts made a fairly concerning decision regarding superstar Shohei Ohtani, who seems to be dealing with a plethora of injuries at the moment.

Ohtani is still working through a lingering knee issue that has kept him away from pitching since before the All-Star break, but he remains in the lineup as a hitter.

However, he missed Thursday's game while dealing with what seems to be a biceps and neck issue, according to Roberts. Now, he'll miss his second consecutive game in the series opener against the Nationals.

He went 0-for-4 with four strikeouts on Wednesday, the last time we saw him play, and he grimaced after his last at-bat, clearly showing signs of discomfort.

This marks the first time all season that Ohtani has missed back-to-back games.

He's logged 499 at-bats this season and is currently batting .279 with 139 hits, 30 home runs and 80 RBIs while slugging .525 with a .906 OPS.

In the games he's pitched, Ohtani has an 8-2 record with a 1.79 ERA across 14 starts and 85.2 innings.

title: CB South edged by Downingtown West in Week 2 football
description: Central Bucks South, with co-coaches, falls to Downingtown West in rematch of 2023 PIAA Class 6A District One championship game.
fullText:
WARRINGTON — When Central Bucks South head coach Tom Hetrick resigned in late July for family health reasons, defensive coordinator Johnny Cataldo and offensive coordinator Bart Szarko became the Titans' co-coaches.

Cataldo and Szarko, who was the first head coach at CB South (from 2004-09), led the Titans for the first time as a tandem in a 35-17 Week 1 football loss to Archbishop Wood.

"We've all been together many years, so the logistics went well," said Cataldo earlier this week. "(There's a) lot to learn and improve on in preparing for this week."

On Friday night, CB South fell to visiting Downingtown West 28-20 in a non-league game.

Downingtown West, which lost its opener 51-20 to Bethlehem Freedom, went 8-3 last year and reached the District One 6A playoffs, while the Titans ended up 5-5.

CB South defeated Downingtown West 27-7 for the 2023 District One 6A championship at Titan Stadium.

Check back later for much more on the game.

The Whippets visit Owen J. Roberts on Sept. 10 (7 p.m.).

The Titans visit Souderton on Sept. 10 (7 p.m.).

title: ‘End of an Era,’ ‘I’m in Shambles’ – Charles Barkley’s Surprise ‘Inside the NBA’ Announcement Leaves Basketball World Emotional
description: Surprising news came down the NBA pipeline on Friday, September 4, when reports circulated that Charles Barkley expects the upcoming 2026–27 season to be his final season on “Inside the NBA. ” He also revealed that longtime host Ernie Johnson might also step away from the show after the season.
fullText:
Surprising news came down the NBA pipeline on Friday, September 4, when reports circulated that Charles Barkley expects the upcoming 2026–27 season to be his final season on "Inside the NBA."

He also revealed that longtime host Ernie Johnson might also step away from the show after the season.

Johnson turned 70 in August. Barkley is 63 himself and has made it clear in the past that he is not trying to work for much longer.

The news led to reactions from several social media users.

Barkley's comments came via the September 3 episode of "The Bill Simmons Podcast," where he mentioned he plans to retire if Johnson does, saying the two are a "package deal." While it's possible they change their minds, fans believe their leaving could be the end of an era.

One fan lamented the news with a strong statement.

"This is the death of Inside the NBA as we know it," Jacob Hitzwrote. "I'm in shambles."

The sentiment was echoed by another user as well,who said: "End of an era. They should just cancel the show when Chuck and Ernie depart."

"Inside the NBA" aired on selected dates after the move to ESPN and ABC last season, with TNT Sports continuing to produce the show. That alone marked a big change in the show's schedule.

One fan noted how that move to ESPN felt like the beginning of the end.

"ESPN really took a lot out of the soul of this show,"they began. "I think people will be fine with it being discontinued now. It was painful to watch last season, but I won't lie, it was cool to see them cover an NBA Finals."

Another usercalled out ESPN for the same thing, speculating: "I knew it wouldn't last long after the ESPN transition. Shaq and Kenny will stay on for paychecks, but it's effectively dead in spirit after Chuck and Ernie leave."

One die-hard welcomed the possibility of a new generation taking the lead.

"I appreciate that he isn't hanging on any longer,"they wrote. "Let the new generation take the lead. I wish more would take that approach."

Some of the users found the possibility to be sad news, as a fun era of NBA coverage could be coming to an end. A fansummed up his emotions regarding the news with: "So this sucks."

MORE: 'Caught a Body,' 'Peak Insecurity' — NBA World Explodes As Tyrese Haliburton 'Claps Back' at Frustrated Bucks Fan

While Johnson has not publicly announced his retirement at the time of reporting, Barkley seems to believe this could be the pair's final season with the show.

This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network.

title: Seahawks Tryout Speedy Ex-Jaguars WR
description: The Seattle Seahawks held a tryout for wide receiver Chandler Brayboy and five other players on Friday. The post Seahawks Tryout Speedy Ex-Jaguars WR appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Seattle Seahawks held tryouts for six players to end this week. All of them were offensive players, including three wide receivers.

According to the NFL transaction wire, one of those wideouts was former Jacksonville Jaguars undrafted receiver Chandler Brayboy. He joined fellow wideouts Luke Floriea and Marcus Sanders Jr. at the workout.

Guard Evan Beerntsen, tackle Tristan Leigh and tight end Layne Pryor also tried out for the Seahawks.

Brayboy has spent the first two summers of his NFL career with the Jaguars. Jacksonville cut him at the end of the 2025 and 2026 preseasons.

During the regular season last year, Brayboy was on the Jaguars practice squad.

At his pro day before the 2025 draft, he ran the 40-yard dash in 4.47 seconds. NFL.com's Lance Zierlein commended Brayboy for his speed and athleticism during the draft process.

"Brayboy's athletic traits warrant a peek at the tape. He has good top-end speed and really impresses with his ability to separate from coverage," Zierlein wrote. "However, his ball skills fall well below NFL standards with spotty ball-tracking and inconsistent hands. He's fearless and fast in a straight line, though.

"His potential as a kick returner will need to be his entry point toward getting a chance in the NFL."

The wideout play college football at Elon in North Carolina. Although the school is an FCS program, Brayboy excelled, becoming a first-team FCS All-American during his final collegiate season.

He also received accolades from his conference during his six-year college career. In 2024, he received the CAA Special teams Player of the Year award.

Brayboy has yet to dress for an NFL regular season game. But he has received a taste of the NFL with the Jaguars.

The same is the case for Floriea, who was also an undrafted free agent in 2025. Floriea has spent the past two training camps with the Cleveland Browns. He received playing time with quarterback Shedeur Sanders during the preseason last year.

Sanders was an undrafted free agent this year. He spent the summer with the Minnesota Vikings.

The Seahawks have five wide receivers on their active roster — Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Rashid Shaheed, Cooper Kupp, Tory Horton and Montorie Foster Jr. With that group, it's unlikely Seattle is interested in signing one of the receivers that tried out for the team Friday to its active roster.

But perhaps a practice squad addition is possible. The Seahawks have receivers Emmanuel Henderson Jr., Julian Hicks and Ricky White III on the practice squad entering Labor Day weekend.

The Seahawks are pretty clearly looking for some potential insurance on offense.

That makes sense. While the team did lose safety Bud Clark to injury during the preseason, the Seahawks will begin 2026 with wide receiver Jake Bobo, offensive lineman Mason Richman and tackle Amari Kight on injured reserve. The team also has another wideout and two full backs on IR.

The Baltimore Ravens picked Beerntsen in the seventh round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Baltimore waived the rookie Sunday.

Leigh was an undrafted free agent who, like Sanders, signed with Vikings. He signed with Minnesota's practice squad after roster cuts, but the Vikings waived him from the practice squad the following day.

Pryor was with the Houston Texans practice squad for most of last season. He was an undrafted free agent in 2025.

title: Michigan Football: All-American Expected to Return for Opener, Expectations Abound
description: For the first time since their 2025 Citrus Bowl loss to the Texas Longhorns, the Michigan Wolverines will be back on the football field this weekend. They’ll be led for the first time by former Utah football coach Kyle Whittingham, but he’s not the only fresh face coming from the Intermountain West.All-American EDGE John Henry […] The post Michigan Football: All-American Expected to Return for Opener, Expectations Abound appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
For the first time since their 2025 Citrus Bowl loss to the Texas Longhorns, the Michigan Wolverines will be back on the football field this weekend. They'll be led for the first time by former Utah football coach Kyle Whittingham, but he's not the only fresh face coming from the Intermountain West.

All-American EDGE John Henry Daley is another of several Utah transplants. And after ending his 2025 campaign on a sour note with a ruptured Achilles, the senior transfer is expected to play in Michigan's season opener against Western Michigan at the Big House on Saturday.

At his first in-season press conference at the helm of the Wolverines on Monday, Whittingham described the standout pass rusher — who logged 48 tackles and 11.5 sacks in a slightly abridged year with the Utes — as "100% ready to roll."

While the excitement surrounding Daley's potential — and defensive coordinator Jay Hill's defense at large — is palpable in Ann Arbor, questions remain. Just over nine months have passed since Daley suffered his injury without contact during a Big 12 battle between Utah and Kansas State. Since then, the Wolverines have been careful to limit Daley's reps during fall camp.

Despite the caution surrounding Daley's situation, though, Whittingham and Hill appear bullish on his ability to play impactful football, with both coaches spotlighting physical improvements in his game.

On Monday, Whittingham said Daley is "probably more explosive and quicker than he's ever been." Hill echoed those sentiments later in the week and praised Michigan's staff for its handling of his injury.

"He's stronger than he's been. He's still coming off an injury, so … Coach [Lewis] Powell's done a great job of just monitoring that injury to where we've got to get him back, but we expect him to be full go," Hill told reporters during a Wednesday press conference.

"I've seen John Henry in person, and then I've played against him or coached against him. So, he's a really, really good player when he's fully healthy and going. And we expect him to be going."

Before his 2025 breakout, Daley split his previous two seasons with Utah and BYU. He logged just four tackles and a sack in 2024 with Utah after appearing in three games as a freshman for the Cougars the prior year.

As Hill seeks to integrate new players and old while also instituting a new — albeit familiar — defensive scheme, having the team's best players on the field and lineup consistency will be crucial. To that end, another key cog — safety Rod Moore — is expected to play in the opener as well.

Moore missed the entire 2024 season with an ACL injury, then aggravated it again early last season. The sixth-year senior and three-time Wolverines captain has 147 career tackles and 7 interceptions.

He and junior safety Chris Bracy will be counted on to anchor a Michigan secondary that Hill and cornerbacks coach Jernaro Gilford expect to be one of the nation's best.

title: Liverpool's Iraola: A fit Isak will 'produce the numbers'
description: Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has no doubt Liverpool's £125 million ($169 million) forward Alexander Isak will "produce the numbers" this season after a brace inside nine minutes inspired a 2-0 win at Ipswich. All eyes were on summer arrival Bradley Barcola in Suffolk, but after Iraola named the France forward on the bench, Isak showed why the Reds paid such a hefty fee to prize him away from Newcastle last summer.
fullText:
Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has no doubt Liverpool's £125 million ($169 million) forward Alexander Isak will "produce the numbers" this season after a brace inside nine minutes inspired a 2-0 win at Ipswich.

All eyes were on summer arrival Bradley Barcola in Suffolk, but after Iraola named the France forward on the bench, Isak showed why the Reds paid such a hefty fee to prize him away from Newcastle last summer.

Isak endured an injury-hit debut campaign at Anfield in which he scored only four goals in 22 appearances, but his double at Portman Road took the 26-year-old up to three for the campaign to help new Liverpool boss Iraola get his first win at the third time of asking.

"Yes, with Alex, if he is fit, if he is available, if he is in good shape, I think he will produce the numbers," Iraola said.

"My demands with Alex will not be about the goals, probably will be about other things. I will demand other things so we can play well, because if we play well we are in good positions and the goals will come.

"He has to contribute towards the collective and knowing when everyone helps, after the goals and assists will come."

Isak stole the headlines on Friday, but both of his strikes were assisted by Cody Gakpo, who could have left Anfield before the transfer deadline, with both Tottenham and Manchester City interested in the Netherlands international.

However, Liverpool blocked a move and Iraola was not surprised by the quality on show from the versatile winger, who produced a fine through-ball for Isak's opener and an even better outside-of-the-foot pass for the second in the ninth-minute.

Iraola added: "I had no doubt with Cody. He has been very good all the pre-season, has started very well the season, producing numbers.

"After the two assists, he finished as a number nine to help us close the game and I think it's good to have Cody because he can play in the three positions up top. To have him in this place, for the beginning of the season, it's good.

"I think Cody knows how much we value him, I think there is no doubt. I rate him very highly."

title: Darian Mensah, Malachi Toney light up Heisman reel on 1st Miami drives
description: The first drive of the 2026 college football season showed why the Miami Hurricanes have two Heisman contenders in Darian Mensah and Malachi Toney.
fullText:
It didn't take long for Miami Hurricanes fans to see what the Darian Mensah to Malachi Toney connection might look like in 2026.

Toney torched the record books in his freshman season, setting school records with 109 catches for 1,211 yards as a freshman. And Mensah finished second in the nation with 3,973 passing yards and 34 touchdowns for Duke, pairing that with just six interceptions.

Mensah replaced Carson Beck for the national runners-up this year, and both entered the season with viable Heisman campaigns. And on the first drive of the first game against Stanford, it became clear that those early projections were not overblown.

On the opening play, Mensah found Toney on a perfect stick route for a 48-yard catch-and-run. Toney nearly sprung a game-opening touchdown, but the sideline limited his escape options from a downfield tackle.

First play of the season and Malachi Toney is already cooking DBspic.twitter.com/umxMgznVjT

He didn't have to wait long for that TD though. After two more plays (and another catch), Mensah hung on through a hit to the head to deliver a beauty of a floater to a wide-open Toney for a 23-yard TD.

It never gets old 😮‍💨🔥

📺: ESPN pic.twitter.com/4oV9lW8FzL

Toney celebrated by hitting the Heisman pose. On the opening drive alone, he had three catches for 75 yards and a score.

But that wasn't all! On Miami's second possession, Toney found the end zone again, working the overmatched cornerback to get open on a 2-yard slant at the goal line. He once again celebrated by hitting the Heisman.

Malachi Toney
5 rec
89 yards
2 TDs pic.twitter.com/SQoQsKFUgb

In two drives, that's five catches for 89 yards and two TDs for Toney. Mensah hasn't been too bad himself, starting 8 of 8 for 129 yards.

title: Probable Formation: Roma vs Atalanta
description: Gasperini should have Dybala and Ndicka ready to go after some minor ailments. Meanwhile, Mora could return to the XI.
fullText:
"We need to take it match by match. It's true that these games are all close together but it's impossible to predict what will happen on the pitch. We've gone months with no injuries, but when you start playing in the league and then the Champions League too, a few players are bound to pick up knocks. We just have to hope they're not serious injuries. You can plan to rest one player or another, but it doesn't always work that way. What I try to do is if someone is tired, I'll bring on someone who's in great form. Some decisions are made with that in mind. We can't always say that a player has had a bump. But when there are longer-term injuries, there's not much we can do."

That was how Gian Piero Gasperini responded to a question about possible lineup changes ahead of Roma's match against Atalanta at the Olimpico on Saturday. With Roma's much-anticipated Champions League return coming on Thursday in Turkey, Gasperini has some time between matches that should allow him to avoid heavy rotation.

However, Gasperini could be cautious with two of his most important players: Evan Ndicka and Paulo Dybala. Ndicka was originally listed as a starter last Monday but had to withdraw due to discomfort before kick-off. Meanwhile, Gianluca DiMarzio reported early on Friday that Dybala was dealing with muscular fatigue. That was ruled minor, and Dybala participated fully in training on the eve of the match. Gasperini updated Dybala and Ndicka's statuses.

"Nothing out of the ordinary. The tests didn't show anything. He'll [Dybala] be training today. The important thing is that he feels confident and comfortable because we've got three games this week. They're all important fixtures and we need to be on top form."

"Ndicka is a lot better. I think he can play. We'll try him in training today."

One player that Gasperini did rule out for the time being is Lorenzo Pellegrini as he gets up to match fitness.

"Pellegrini? He's started to work with the group a bit. As for playing a match, maybe against Inter or after the break."

He also discussed the roles of two of his youngest players—Rodrigo Mora and Niccolo Pisilli—who have both already found their names on the scoresheet in the first two matches of the season, while also discussing whether or not he has a midfield hierarchy.

"He's [Mora] played two games in two. Whether he's in the starting XI or on the bench, it's not that someone who starts is a starting XI player and someone that gets subbed on is a substitute. It's true that he's young but he's already shown he's talented in the games against Fiorentina and Lecce. He's very young and has plenty of room to grow in terms of his physical condition, stamina and endurance. We're dealing with a player of exceptional quality – that's hard to deny."

"Pisilli is well ahead. He's matured, gained self-awareness, he's grown and he's a strong player. I've got four players there. I don't do hierarchies. De Roon, [Leonardo] Balerdi and the new signings need to get into peak condition. They'll come on for spells, and we'll probably see them play a full game after the international break because they haven't been here long. Pisilli, [Manu] Kone and [Bryan] Cristante are solid – there's no hierarchy there. If someone's fatigued, then whoever's in better shape will play, as I said before. Maybe in a month's time someone else will play more but they're all part of the game regardless. We've got 16 players and there are lots of matches. Don't make any distinctions between those that start and those who come on because, in the end, you'll see that playing time will be similar for everyone."

He also lauded Matías Soulé's hot start to the season.

"Soule's groin injury is a distant memory. He's made an outstanding recovery and he's doing well."

Lastly, Gasperini was asked whether we could see one trequartista behind two strikers as he's played in the past against a four man defense, which would mean Malen and Castro playing together.

"Sure. They're all versatile players who can adapt to different tactical systems. The more Castro and Mora play, the better they'll be able to fit into the team but there are no problems with the other players either."

With five days ahead of the match in Turkey, Gasperini shouldn't be forced into too many changes from Monday's match in Lecce. And if Ndicka and Dybala are ready, they should be given the go from the jump. If they're not deemed fit to start then expect Daniele Ghilardi and Matías Soulé to take their respective spots.

ROMA (3-4-2-1): Svilar; Mancini, Ndicka, Hermoso; Lulli, Koné, Cristante, Wesley; Dybala, Mora; Malen.

title: Moments: Braves 5, Phillies 2
description: Did everyone have fun?
fullText:
Through the first seven innings of this game, it had the feeling of a true battle between teams with margins as thin as paper. Both starters, Chris Sale and Cristopher Sánchez, labored through five innings at exactly 88 pitches, faced sixth-inning jams before escaping unscathed with a 3-2 Braves lead for the late innings. Both teams even brought in rookie right-handed flamethrowers who threw scoreless seventh innings on eight pitches. It's sort of crazy when you think about it.

Sometimes the differences, even if they only last for a single game, are defined by a few moments.

The second inning would feature several of these moments. The Braves failed to capitalize on a leadoff Ronald Acuña Jr. double in the first but were ready to rally an inning later. Lane Thomas started it off by working a six pitch walk, then Mauricio Dubón pulled a changeup right past the gloves and Edmundo Sosa and Trea Turner for a base hit into left field.

After a Sean Murphy strikeout, Austin Riley was ready to punch a changeup into a vacated hole between first and second base to bring Thomas home, the ball went right under Bryce Harper's glove in right field, leading to Dubón taking third base.

That moment would matter when Ha-Seong Kim, who entered the game hitting .120 with a .344 OPS, did what he could against a Sánchez changeup for a groundout that scored a run.

On the very next pitch, Acuña took a first pitch changeup to center field for a base hit that brought in a third run to make it 3-0.

The Phillies answered right back in the bottom half, Luis Arraez punched a single into left field and on the very next pitch, Alec Bohm took a hanging slider to the center field wall to cut the Braves lead down to two.

After Edmundo Sosa got hit with a backfoot slider, the Phillies were just not able to capitalize off Sale. Bryan De La Cruz grounded into a double play, then JT Realmuto went down swinging on a backfoot slider.

These were not the last situations each of the aces had to escape from but in the in-between, Alec Bohm smoked a fastball for a line drive home run to cut the Braves lead in half.

A Rav4th Inning Bohment brings us within one@Toyota x #RingTheBell pic.twitter.com/7QSTrVCgvE

In the bottom of the fifth, the Phillies had the chance to build on their budding momentum over the last few innings. Sánchez escaped the top half of the fifth by getting Matt Olson to flyout after an Ozzie Albies two out double.

After a Realmuto walk and a pair of flyouts, Trea Turner took a high fastball near the foul line in left field that put runners on second and third with two outs and Bryce Harper to the plate. Harper, who entered tonight with a 35 game on-base streak, was unable to deliver and hit a pop up to Austin Riley at third base.

The sixth inning is probably what will haunt the Phillies the most for the night. Arraez smoked a hanging slider off the wall in right field for a leadoff double with three straight right-handed hitters behind him to face a tired Sale.

Alec Bohm, who had seen Chris Sale very well in his first two at-bats, grounded out to third base, keeping Arraez at second. Edmundo Sosa swung at two backfoot sliders in a row and walked back to the dugout. Bryan De La Cruz had a clear plan against Sale, looking for a high fastball but fouling the 1-0 heater. He took consecutive down-and-in sliders but one of them was barely a strike. After an uncompetitive slider made the count 3-2, De La Cruz was late on a hanging slider and went down swinging to end the inning.

After scoreless seventh innings from two rookie relievers, Alex McFarlane and Didier Fuentes, Orion Kerkering came in for the eighth to try and keep the game close. With one out, Kerkering walked Mike Yastrzemski on eight pitches that sent Mauricio Dubón up. On the second pitch of the at-bat, Kerkering hung a sweeper that Dubón crushed, into the left-field seats, sealing Atlanta's fate.

Dubón delivers! 💣 pic.twitter.com/upxSobc61i

After Fuentes and Raisel Iglesias were able to retire the next hitters, the Braves muscled a 5-2 victory to start the wraparound Labor Day series.

The gaps between these teams look thin, but maybe that is just because of the starting pitching matchup. Whatever it is, the Phillies will need them to break their way for three straight games if they want to have any real chance at their third straight division title.

title: NBA Insider Reveals Potential Problem For Lakers Ahead Of 2026-27 Season
description: Tensions could rise in Los Angeles as Lakers juggle two different timelines.
fullText:
On paper, the Los Angeles Lakers have more than enough to keep up with the NBA's most elite teams. Even without LeBron James, the combined efforts of Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves should put the Lakers firmly in the playoff mix, and they have every intention of getting as far as they can.

Even so, one NBA insider noted a very interesting challenge facing this Lakers team, and specifically head coach JJ Redick. Somehow, Reddick will have to find a way to balance maximizing the performance of the roster while giving young players like Adou Thiero, Bronny James, and Cameron Carr a chance to shine. It's a slippery slope that could have drastic consequences if mishandled.

"I do think Jake [LaRavia], whether he starts or comes off the bench, is going to factor into the rotation. JJ showed it last year; he started half the season," said insider Jovan Buha. "I think Jake will play, but I think this is one of the minor tensions of the Lakers' season is you want to develop a dude in Cameron Carr. At the same time, you're in win-now mode. This is not like a rebuilding season, this is not another gap year, this is not a let's just see what we have in Adou and Carr, and let the chips fall where they may.' No, you're trying to win a championship this year, and you're trying to show Luka Doncic that it's worth signing that extension next summer. So, that's the tension here of who will help the Lakers win more tomorrow vs who will help the Lakers win more in a year. How do you negotiate that, and that's something the NBA will have to figure out."

In the modern NBA, building contending teams is harder than ever, and it often requires years of planning, posturing, and buildup just to make it happen. In the Lakers' case, the arrival of Luka Doncic in 2025 essentially reset their championship window, thrusting them into win-now mode with added pressure to keep Doncic happy.

His presence is why the Lakers traded for Walker Kessler and why they gave Austin Reaves that massive contract extension. Collectively, the Lakers believe their new star-studded trio is one of the best in the game, and expectations are running high ahead of their first season together.

What often gets overlooked, however, is the Lakers' plan to build for the future. As much as they want to win now, building and developing their own young players has become an increasingly important matter, especially with how many they have. Between Cameron Carr, Adou Thiero, Bronny James, and Dalton Knecht, the Lakers could see some major internal improvement if they provide the right opportunities to their young core.

The challenge for head coach JJ Redick is deciding how to incorporate the young players into the win-now roster. There's no clear-cut answer, and some feelings could get hurt, but Redick is a man of results, and he will likely give more opportunities to the young guys who make the biggest impact on the floor. Either way, JJ Redick must navigate this issue carefully, as any wrong step could damage team chemistry and locker room morale.

title: Jones’ Gem, Griffin’s Speed Lead Pirates Past Angels; Playoff Hopes Still Alive?
description: PITTSBURGH — Jared Jones had one of his best starts since returning from elbow surgery, and Konnor Griffin made his […]
fullText:
PITTSBURGH — Jared Jones had one of his best starts since returning from elbow surgery, and Konnor Griffin made his presence known in his first game off the IL as the Pirates beat the Angels 1-0 at PNC Park on Friday night.

Bottom 2nd, 1-0 PIT: Konnor Griffin scored from first base on Jake Mangum's double to right field off Ryan Johnson (3-8). Griffin stumbled around third but slid head first into home to just beat the throw and give the Pirates (70-72) the advantage.

The KG impact. 🏃‍♂️‍➡️ pic.twitter.com/A3Kh8hHeGF

Jared Jones (3-6) didn't have to work from the stretch much, but he wiggled out of a big jam in the second inning. The Angels (53-88) had runners on the corners with no outs, but Jones prevented a run from scoring thanks to a foul out and a pair of punchouts.

Jared Jones threw a season-high 91 pitches and matched a season-high with six innings and nine strikeouts. He blanked the Angels on three hits and only one walk.

The Pirates had lost each of Jared Jones' last seven starts dating back to the first game of a doubleheader in Cleveland on July 18. Jones had gone 0-5 during that time.

Jared Jones: 6.0 innings, three hits, no runs, one walk, nine strikeouts, 91 pitches/63 strikes

Wilber Dotel: 2.0 innings, two hits, no runs, one walk, two strikeouts, 34 pitches/24 strikes

Bryan Reynolds: 2 for 4, one double

Jake Mangum: 1 for 3, one double, one RBI

The Pirates improved to 7-3 over their last 10 games.

Mason Montgomery notched his ninth save of the season.

The Pirates reinstated SS Konnor Griffin from the 60-day injured list. C Christian Bethancourt was designated for assignment. Additionally, the Pirates recalled RHP Isaac Mattson from Triple-A Indianapolis and optioned LHP Brandon Eisert.

Prior to the start of the game, the Pirates honored their 2026 Hall of Fame inductees in a pregame ceremony. The class consists of SS Jack Wilson, LHP John Candelaria and LHP Wilbur Cooper.

RHP Braxton Ashcraft (14-5, 3.59 ERA) starts for the Pirates in the second game of the series on Saturday night. LHP Yusei Kikuchi (0-5, 5.65 ERA) gets the ball for the Angels. First pitch: 6:40 p.m. ET on SportsNet Pittsburgh/93.7 The Fan.

title: Angels get blanked by Pirates, waste Johnson's strong outing
description: Right-hander Ryan Johnson continues his hot stretch on the mound, but the offense failed to score in their 1-0 loss against the Pirates.
fullText:
The Angels continue to pair great pitching performances with poor offensive production.

The latest case was the Angels' 1-0 loss against the Pirates on Friday night, as right-hander Ryan Johnson's six innings of one-run ball were wasted.

Johnson struck out six and allowed only four hits over his six innings, continuing his impressive hot streak. After starting the season with a 7.63 ERA, he's pitched to a 1.67 ERA over his last six starts since the calendar flipped to August.

The cutter and sweeper combination proved to be deadly to the Pirates.

Johnson used his cutter and sweeper to get swings and misses, chases out of the strike zone and he was able to steal strike one with them.

Pirates hitters swung and missed at 39% of Johnson's cutters and 28% of his sweepers.

He landed his cutter for a first-pitch strike 10 out of 12 times, and his sweeper four out of six times. Both pitches may not have been in the strike zone all that often, but because he was able to get hitters to chase out of the zone, both pitches ended up being strikes at almost an 80% clip.

The only run Johnson allowed was back in the second inning, when Konnor Griffin scored from first base on a double down the right-field line by Jake Magnum. After that, Johnson only allowed two baserunners to reach scoring position the rest of the outing.

All of Johnson's work was essentially wasted, though, because the Angels couldn't find an answer for any pitcher the Pirates sent to the mound.

Whittier native right-hander Jared Jones struck out nine Angels over six shutout innings on three hits. Right-hander Wilber Dotel then shut down the Angels for two scoreless innings with a pair of strikeouts. Left-hander Mason Montgomery came in and closed it out in the ninth.

The Angels' offense as a whole struck out 11 times and only recorded three hits. Only one baserunner reached scoring position when Vaughn Grissom got to third base with no outs in the second inning, but the Angels went popout, strikeout and strikeout to end the threat.

title: Sweet victory - Sturgis beats BC Pennfield to end 20-game losing streak
description: Road victory on Thursday ends lengthy losing skid for Sturgis football
fullText:
BATTLE CREEK — The victory bell at Sturgis High School sat silent for a quite a while.

But on Thursday evening, the bell rang out, sending waves throughout the community as the Trojans returned home from Battle Creek with a victory. The black and orange hit the road and knocked off Battle Creek Pennfield, 27-8. It ended a 20-game losing streak by Sturgis, which previously won on Oct. 13, 2023 over Three Rivers, 13-12.

Sturgis nearly won on opening night last week, falling to Coldwater 21-20 in overtime. The defense played well in that one, but ultimately came up just short of claiming victory.

THURSDAY WINS: Mendon, Marcellus football pick up impressive wins Thursday

WEST, FALLS LEAD COLON: West, Falls help Colon seal victory over Adrian Lenawee Christian

In their second game of the year, the Trojans were once again tough on defense. The Trojans went three-plus quarters without allowing a point.

Sturgis' defense actually scored before the offense did in the game. Melachi Warner intercepted a pass and ran it back for a score, it was a 43-yard touchdown right before the half.

The Trojans scored once more before the half as well. It came on a 7-yard run from Cristian Alvez which made it 13-0 following the extra point.

A pair of TDs in the third quarter gave the Trojans some security. The first was a 13-yard pass from Beckett Lamb to Hudson Lamb. On the ensuing drive following an interception, Beckett Lamb motored 40 yards to the house to give the Trojans a four-score lead.

Alvez finished with 87 yards on the ground, Beckett Lamb ran for 57. Kevin Naliwajko added 28 yards on the ground as well. Beckett Lamb completed three-of-five passes for 49 yards. Hudson Lamb caught two for 24, Darren Speelman hauled in one for 25.

Beckett Lamb led the defense with 7.5 stops, Hudson Lamb was in on 6.5 stops, as was Liam McKinley. Warner added five tackles, plus the interception for a TD. McKinley, Naliwajko and Speelman each intercepted a pass as well.

Sturgis hits the road again this coming week, traveling to take on Edwardsburg.

title: Aryna Sabalenka disturbed by weed during US Open match: ‘It’s so strong’

fullText:
World No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka cruised to a straight set victory over Kamilla Rakhimova to reach the Round of 16 at the 2026 US Open on Friday. Well, there was one hiccup for the reigning back-to-back US Open champion.

Early in the first set, Sabalenka walked over to the chair umpire. The broadcast captured her saying, "Someone is smoking weed. Do you mind? Because it's so strong."

“Someone is smoking weed. Do you mind? Because it’s so strong.” – Aryna Sabalenka to the umpire during the US Open

Sabalenka (No. 1) won the third-round match 6-3, 6-4. pic.twitter.com/8JIftNUPpf

— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) September 4, 2026

The weed metaphorically wafted into Sabalenka's post-match press conference, as questions about it dominated her 10-minute media availability.

"I was like, guys, you can do whatever," Sabalenka, a four-time Grand Slam champion, said through laughter. "You can smoke whatever. You can relax as much as you can, but please do not do it around the tennis courts. It's a bit tricky to handle that smell while you're trying to compete at your best."

A few questions later, a different reporter asked Sabalenka for her immediate reaction when she smelled weed. Again, she laughed, and said, "Come on, guys. I think there is nothing else to say about weed. I'm just asking people not to smoke it next to the tennis court."

Not deterred in the slightest, the same reporter asked whether Friday marked Sabalenka's first whiff of weed while playing at the US Open. "That strong? Yeah," she said. "Also because it was a bit windy. I don't know if it was coming from the crowd or the outside because wind blows it into the stadium. I just hope they're gonna be a bit more aware of that stuff."

Eventually, the press did move on to tennis-centric talk, but Sabalenka hilariously misunderstood one question as another one about marijuana.

"How much of a high are you on here compared to the other majors?" Craig Gabriel asked.

Sabalenka, visibly perplexed, asked him to repeat the question, which he did. "A high? The level?" Sabalenka asked. "Now, I can only hear the weird stuff! If they're gonna keep smoking, I might get high."

After a fit of laughter in the room, Sabalenka confirmed that she is typically most comfortable at the US Open and loves competing in New York City. She'll next face Taylor Townsend on Sunday in pursuit of a historic US Open three-peat.

title: Boise State state football experiencing travel issues ahead of Oregon matchup
description: Boise State was unable to fly into Eugene, Oregon and will have to take a bus from Portland for a late night arrival a day before it plays Oregon.
fullText:
Boise State will open the 2026 season against No. 2 Oregon on Saturday, Sept. 5, but the big weekend got off to a bumpy start.

The Broncos are dealing with travel issues that have made for a long day trying to get to Eugene, Oregon due to weather. The team was scheduled to fly into Eugene Airport in the afternoon of Friday, Sept. 4, but were unable to land after multiple attempts to do, according to Flight Radar data. The attempt came as it was raining in the area.

Ultimately, the plane was diverted to Portland International Airport, landing around 3 p.m. local time, hoping to eventually fly down to Eugene after the brief stop. However, weather was also an issue in Portland, resulting in the team not able to get in the sky again, and instead having to take a bus down to Eugene, Boise State confirmed to USA TODAY Sports.

As of 6 p.m. PT, the team hadn't left on the busses for the roughly two hour drive from Portland to Eugene, meaning the Boise State squad will still be traveling well into the night. The earliest the Broncos could be arriving at their team hotel is at 9 p.m.

It's certainly not the way Boise State wanted to start the campaign, especially considering the Broncos and Ducks kick off at 12:30 p.m. local time, meaning it will have to be up quite early after a long travel day results in a longer night.

Boise State is starting its first season as a Pac-12 member in the rebranded conferences, and will try to win its first game at Autzen Stadium since 2008, owning a 3-1 record all-time against Oregon.

title: Claude Fable 5.1 vs. GPT-6 Astra, who wins on the 3D modeling?
description: worlds via code, from fable 5.1. Contribute to PhiloLabs/fable51-worlds development by creating an account on GitHub.
fullText:
Worlds as code. A prompt in, a world you can walk out.

Claude Fable 5.1 agent swarms take a brief - a sentence, a photograph, a clip - then research the place, model it, render it, and check it. What ships is a plain Three.js app that opens in a browser.

No game engine. No proprietary 3D tiles. No downloaded meshes. Every building, storefront, sign, tree and traffic light is generated by code that lives in this repo.

Same brief, same test conditions, two models. Each built Union Square from scratch, then the Astra world was filmed along the Fable walkthrough's camera route and the two are shown side by side, unedited.

▶ Watch the head-to-head · 59 s · left GPT-6 Astra, right Claude Fable 5.1 · Fable 5.1 build · GPT-6 Astra build

▶ Watch the walkthrough · 59 s · 1920×1080 · aerial, plaza, Nintendo, lower level, Apple

▶ Watch the walkthrough · 54 s · 1920×1080 · seven scenes, Gion to Kiyomizu-dera at sunset

Text, video or image. The brief names the subject and the style, and the same pipeline runs behind all three.

Style is as open as subject. The same street can come back as a cel-shaded anime plate, a photographic reconstruction or a night scene, because each world's renderer is written for it rather than chosen from a list.

A world is the substrate. What stands on it is the point.

Every stage is in the repo, and every stage can be re-run:

A world written as code is not the same kind of object as a world generated as pixels or held in a latent space.

title: A Movie Can't Be Just Its Own Thing Anymore
description: The new film “Onslaught” suggests that everyone is itching for sequels—and not to viewers’ benefit.
fullText:
Onslaught, in theaters this week, should be the perfect early-September treat. The aggressive action thriller is gory, loud, and packed with interesting actors, and it has a straightforward premise: Three murderous super-soldiers, the result of some shadowy extra-governmental experiment, have escaped from a lab and are descending upon a small town in New Mexico. A tough-as-nails retired Army sniper named Celeste (played by Adria Arjona), living somewhat off the grid in a trailer park, must use her grit and know-how to defend herself against the oncoming attack. Yet as simple as that sounds, the film feels needlessly complex. Rather than just delivering on its clean setup, it becomes fixated on teasing future installments—a symptom of the obsession with sequelization that’s affecting even smaller genre films.

The director Adam Wingard was, once upon a time, a master of the cheap thrill. This is a compliment; he emerged from the micro-budget mumblecore scene in the 2000s, then made two impressively nasty bits of horror—the slasher You’re Next and the wonderfully tawdry and tense The Guest. But Wingard has spent years trapped in franchise drudgery, offering up an unnecessary follow-up to The Blair Witch Project and a pair of giant-scale, instantly forgettable Godzilla movies. Onslaught initially suggests a more back-to-basics turn for the director, a return to R-rated indies that are unencumbered by cinematic universes. That mission, however, seems to have been a little corrupted by what Wingard’s been working on in the meantime.

Onslaught begins on a compelling note. Its aesthetics are top-notch, the opening credits unfolding as an invigorating blitz of conspiratorial imagery that cuts together cable-news clips of several presidents, including Richard Nixon, Bill Clinton, and George W. Bush, with drone footage of overseas combat; the entire sequence feels like a fever dream of the early 2000s. Celeste is a veteran of an unspecified overseas combat engagement, and the audience briefly glimpses in flashback the traumatic firefights that preceded her discharge. Living alongside her in the desert trailer park is a crew of other misfits, including the bumbling policeman Kovacks (Eric Wareheim) and a cantankerous older fella named Josiah (Reginald VelJohnson). To Celeste’s annoyance, her ex-husband drops off their cherubic daughter that day to stay the weekend; the tension is, of course, quickly building to a violent incursion.

Read: Hollywood’s star power is shifting

Part of my irritation with the film, though, stems from just how jazzed I felt about its first act. The actor Dan Stevens, at this point a longtime collaborator of Wingard’s (including, most recently, the director’s previous Godzilla movie), dons nightmarish makeup to play Dr. Hans Kammler; he’s a German-speaking mad scientist in charge of the military experiment that goes wrong. Rebecca Hall, another Godzilla alum, is Dr. Kammler’s domineering wife, Hanna—a stiletto-clad, cigarette-smoking badass boasting some mysteriously derived authority. The duo’s cartoonish poise is a delight to witness, as is their ridiculous hubris: Whatever lab simulation they’ve designed for their seemingly zombified super-soldiers quickly falls apart, leading the latter to invade the surrounding environs.

Some solid gunplay follows, and the final showdown between Celeste and her trailer-park buds and the soldiers has some brutal flourishes—though it irritatingly takes place at night, making the chaos a little harder to see. But the screenplay (written by Simon Barrett) teases revelations throughout, then delivers on practically none of them. Hanna and Dr. Kammler’s work remains nebulous, and Celeste’s backstory is only vaguely filled in. These gaps would be forgivable if Onslaught existed mostly to deliver the frivolity that Wingard once excelled at; instead, it ends on a cliff-hanger that hints at further developments. In interviews, the director has even alluded to the movie belonging to a growing shared universe alongside You’re Next and The Guest, though there’s no real on-screen evidence of that.

I am not opposed to Wingard building connections among his works, especially if he’s looking to do it in a more intentional way. Too often, though, Onslaught acts like it’s making moves in that direction without a real sense of purpose. The Godzilla-centric enterprise that Wingard has spent the past few years in, also known as the “Monsterverse,” relies on the kind of lazy storytelling that films designed to spawn numerous sequels tend to tell: Rather than ending punchily, the movie lands on a big conflict that sets up new villains and crossover possibilities. Perhaps Onslaught will be a big enough hit to get a similar treatment, even on a smaller scale. More likely, though, the lack of resolution will leave people feeling as dissatisfied as I did.
