title: To Ruby from Python
description: Python is another very nice general purpose programming language. Goingfrom Python to Ruby, you’ll find that there’s a little bit more syntaxto learn than wi...
fullText:
To Ruby From Python

 Python is another very nice general purpose programming language. Going
from Python to Ruby, you’ll find that there’s a little bit more syntax
to learn than with Python.

Similarities

As with Python, in Ruby,…

 There’s an interactive prompt (called irb).
 You can read docs on the command line (with the ri command instead
of pydoc).
 There are no special line terminators (except the usual newline).
 String literals can span multiple lines like Python’s triple-quoted
strings.
 Brackets are for lists, and braces are for dicts (which, in Ruby, are
called “hashes”).
 Arrays work the same (adding them makes one long array, but composing
them like this a3 = [ a1, a2 ] gives you an array of arrays).
 Objects are strongly and dynamically typed.
 Everything is an object, and variables are just references to objects.
 Although the keywords are a bit different, exceptions work about the
same.
 You’ve got embedded doc tools (Ruby’s is called rdoc).
 There is good support for functional programming with first-class
functions, anonymous functions, and closures.

Differences

Unlike Python, in Ruby,…

 Strings are mutable.
 You can make constants (variables whose value you don’t intend to
change).
 There are some enforced case-conventions (ex. class names start with a
capital letter, variables start with a lowercase letter).
 There’s only one kind of list container (an Array), and it’s mutable.
 Double-quoted strings allow escape sequences (like \t) and a special
“expression substitution” syntax (which allows you to insert the
results of Ruby expressions directly into other strings without having
to "add " + "strings " + "together"). Single-quoted strings are like
Python’s r"raw strings".
 There are no “new style” and “old style” classes. Just one kind.
(Python 3+ doesn’t have this issue, but it isn’t fully backward
compatible with Python 2.)
 You never directly access attributes. With Ruby, it’s all method
calls.
 Parentheses for method calls are usually optional.
 There’s public, private, and protected to enforce access,
instead of Python’s _voluntary_ underscore __convention__.
 “mixins” are used instead of multiple inheritance.
 You can add or modify the methods of built-in classes. Both languages
let you open up and modify classes at any point, but Python prevents
modification of built-ins — Ruby does not.
 You’ve got true and false instead of True and False (and nil
instead of None).
 When tested for truth, only false and nil evaluate to a false
value. Everything else is true (including 0, 0.0, "", and []).
 It’s elsif instead of elif.
 It’s require instead of import. Otherwise though, usage is the
same.
 The usual-style comments on the line(s) above things (instead of
docstrings below them) are used for generating docs.
 There are a number of shortcuts that, although give you more to
remember, you quickly learn. They tend to make Ruby fun and very
productive.
 There’s no way to unset a variable once set (like Python’s del
statement). You can reset a variable to nil, allowing the old
contents to be garbage collected, but the variable will remain in the
symbol table as long as it is in scope.
 The yield keyword behaves differently. In Python it will return
execution to the scope outside the function’s invocation. External
code is responsible for resuming the function. In Ruby yield will
execute another function that has been passed as the final argument,
then immediately resume.
 Python supports just one kind of anonymous functions, lambdas, while
Ruby contains blocks, Procs, and lambdas.

title: The Rise and Fall of the Harper Rule
description: Discover this moment in HarperCollins history. #hc200
fullText:
In the early 1800s, American printers had no qualms about pirating books from abroad and selling them at discount prices. The Harper brothers of New York were no exception. Their biggest competitor at the time was Mathew Carey’s publishing house of Philadelphia, and throughout the early 1820s a fierce rivalry developed between the publishers, resulting from their often simultaneous publication of the same books.

According to third-generation partner and firm historian J. Henry Harper, “a messenger would board the incoming packet before she was made fast to the wharf to secure as soon as possible the early sheets. Every compositor was then put on the work, and every press stood ready for the printing.” The Harper brothers succeeded in getting Sir Walter Scott’s Peveril of the Peak (1823) printed and bound only twenty-one hours after the packet ship arrived, beating out the Carey firm, which had purchased the advance proofs.

There was a cease-fire in the 1830s when the Harper brothers and Henry Carey, Mathew’s son, reached an agreement known as “The Harper Rule,” in which a publisher would cease printing when a competitor purchased advance proofs and announced forthcoming titles, or had previously published a British author. Long Bets names both parties and lists $20,000 in stakes, payable to the Electronic Frontier Foundation if Kapor wins or the Kurzweil Foundation if Kurzweil wins. The registry establishes acceptance. April 9 is the rules publication date; the exact agreement day has not been established here.

The protocol uses three judges, three human foils, and one computer, with two-hour interviews of each candidate by each judge. The computer must pass both the human-identification and rank-order tests under the published procedure. Settlement depends on the authorized committee and Long Now process. Preserve authorized rule changes and their dates. Other studies using the name "Turing test" require comparison with this protocol before they can count as outcome evidence.

The Kurzweil and Kapor records are opposite sides of one shared event and should retain that relationship. All four entries remain submissions until their sources, current status, and resolution terms have been reviewed.

title: Personal AI Router for Local Inference
description: Route AI inference locally across RTX, DGX, and Mac.
fullText:
The NVIDIA PAIR beta connects AI app and agent workflows to a single local endpoint for routing inference across NVIDIA DGX Spark™, Windows systems with RTX™, and macOS devices. This helps you maximize local compute while keeping prompts, files, and agent context private.

Validated Configurations | FAQs | Support

Bring together the RTX, DGX™, and Mac systems already on your network in minutes. NVIDIA PAIR discovers compatible local machines and helps them work as one personal AI inference cluster with no special cables, racks, or complex cluster setup required.

Keep local AI workflows moving when tasks stack up. NVIDIA PAIR routes AI inference requests across available local nodes, helping busy AI workflows tap into idle compute regardless of the node’s operating system.

Run NVIDIA PAIR alongside familiar local inference backends on Windows, Linux, and macOS. At launch, NVIDIA PAIR supports Ollama and LM Studio, giving apps a consistent, single endpoint while intelligently proxying requests to available local compute.

Run AI workflows at home with data that stays on your network. NVIDIA PAIR is built for private local inference, helping you use prompts, files, and agent context without sending them to the cloud.

NVIDIA PAIR works without special cables or racks. And setting up is easy.

NVIDIA Personal AI Router (PAIR) is software that connects compatible macOS, Windows, and Linux systems with NVIDIA RTX™GPUs and DGX Spark systems into a personal home AI cluster. PAIR distributes local AI inference workloads across available devices while keeping prompts, files, and agent context on the user’s home network.

A personal home AI cluster connects multiple compatible devices on the same local network, allowing them to share available computing resources for local AI inference. PAIR enables Macs, NVIDIA RTX systems, and DGX Spark systems to provide more capacity for local AI applications and agents. The devices remain separate systems that handle parallel tasks; PAIR doesn’t combine them into one virtual GPU.

Download PAIR, install it on supported systems, pair the devices on the same local network, and add them to the cluster. Once connected, supported applications and agents can send inference requests through the PAIR local endpoint.

NVIDIA PAIR requires compatible macOS, Windows, or Linux systems and supported hardware. Requirements may include specific operating system versions, NVIDIA RTX GPUs, GPU memory, system memory, processors, storage, and local network connectivity. See the System Requirements section on the NVIDIA PAIR landing page for current details.

PAIR is designed for private local inference. Prompts, files, and agent context remain on the user’s local network instead of being sent to a cloud inference service.

title: UN General Assembly endorses a new world map that shows more accurately Africa's size
description: The United Nations General Assembly on Friday endorsed a new world map that represents Africa more accurately in its larger size, a culmination of a recent campaign led by African countries and advoca...
fullText:
The United Nations General Assembly on Friday endorsed a new world map that represents Africa more accurately in its larger size, a culmination of a recent campaign led by African countries and advocacy groups.

Friday's resolution, which was sponsored by Togo and backed by members of the African Union, was passed with 164 member states voting in favor. Only the U.S. voted against it while six other countries — Serbia, Estonia, Georgia, Lithuania, Moldova and Ukraine — abstained.

The vote encourages governments and institutions around the world to replace the traditional Mercator map, commonly used since the 16th Century, with the Equal Earth projection that advocates and geographers say shows locations more accurately.

The Mercator projection shows Greenland and Africa as appearing to be about the same size whereas in the Equal Earth projection that shows continents in their true proportions, Africa is 14 times larger than Greenland.

Friday's resolution does not ban the Mercator projection or impose a replacement, but only encourages the use of the Equal Earth projection, the U.N. said in its report.

"Maps shape our understanding of the world," the global body quoted Togo's Foreign Minister Robert Dussey as saying before the vote. "They guide education, nourish the imagination, and influence collective perceptions."

Africa No Filter, one of the lead campaigners for the adoption of the new map, hailed the resolution, adding: "We want to see accurate maps in schools, textbooks, newsrooms, businesses and on the digital platforms billions of people use every day."

Several countries hailed the adoption and urged the adoption of the Equal Earth map. "Changing the map obviously doesn't change the world. But correcting a representation that distorts it is already an act of truth," French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said on X after the vote.

The Mercator map was designed by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator to help European navigators at sea, but advocates say it distorted landmasses by enlarging regions near the poles such as North America and Greenland while shrinking Africa and South America.

The 2018 Equal Earth projection, on the other hand, follows the Earth's curvature and shows continents in their true proportions.

Geographers say the traditional map is only useful for navigation.

"Outside of that very narrow navigation application, there is no point in using it," according to Mark Monmonier, a Syracuse University professor of geography.

title: Supreme Court grants Republican emergency appeal on TV ad rates before midterms
description: The Supreme Court granted an emergency appeal from Republicans in a dispute over campaign ad prices on Friday, clearing a legal roadblock to political parties getting cheaper TV ad time ahead of the m...
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The Supreme Court granted an emergency appeal from Republicans in a dispute over campaign ad prices on Friday, clearing a legal roadblock to political parties getting cheaper TV ad time ahead of the midterm elections.

The justices halted for now a lower-court ruling in favor of Democratic candidates who argued that cheaper broadcast ads should be limited to candidates. One justice publicly dissented from the unsigned order. It's the latest election-related appeal to come before the high court ahead of the pivotal November contests.

The Trump administration supported the emergency appeal from GOP campaign arms.

The decision comes on the heels of a June Supreme Court ruling that removed limits on parties spending money in coordination with candidates. It was seen as a boon to the GOP because the national party has a sizable cash advantage, and access to cheaper ad rates could boost that edge.

Among Democrats, meanwhile, some individual candidates have sizable fundraising advantages over their Republican opponents.

Candidates pay discounted rates for TV time around an election under federal law, and in March the Federal Communications Commission's Media Bureau said certain party-coordinated ads are entitled to those prices as well.

Four Democrats, including Sen. Jon Ossoff of Georgia and former Sen. Sherrod Brown of Ohio, challenged the finding in court. They won a victory from a divided panel of the U.S. 4th Circuit Court of appeals.

The National Republican Congressional Committee and National Republican Senatorial Committee then asked the Supreme Court to intervene. They argued that broadcasters were already charging them higher rates and upending their planned budgets after the appeals court decision.

The majority of justices agreed that the lower court had acted too soon with the order that differed from judges around the country.

"Current and future recissions will require the party committees to pay more for advertising space, thereby hampering their efforts to reach the electorate in the critical weeks leading up to the midterms," the Supreme Court order states.

One justice, Ketanji Brown Jackson, disagreed, writing that the court likely didn't have to wait until an internal FCC review was done.

The decision halts the appeals court ruling while the Republican committees file a fuller appeal.

title: 10 Hacks Every Proton Mail User Should Know
description: Maximize Proton's privacy features with these tricks.
fullText:
Proton Mail is a privacy-focused mail service that strips trackers from messages, maintains zero-access encryption (meaning Proton can't read or hand over the content of your emails), and offers end-to-end encryption between Proton mailboxes. If you're a Proton user, there are a handful of other hacks you should know to maximize these privacy features and make sending and receiving emails as seamless as possible.

Proton Mail is free to use if you have just one email address, but storage is limited to just 500 MB, which will fill up fast if you are receiving messages with large attachments. You can upgrade to a Plus subscription for $4 per month to get 15 GB of storage—the same amount available to most Google users—but if you don't want to pay anything, you can at least double your limit to 1 GB by completing Proton's onboarding process within 18 days of signing up. Look for a Get more storage option on the left sidebar of your mailbox, and click an action to complete the task. Once you've finished the checklist, you'll unlock an additional 500 MB of storage on your account.

If you have a relatively common name, it's likely that many email addresses using simple conventions, such as firstname.lastname, have already been claimed. By the time your kids are old enough to set up their own accounts, pickings may be even slimmer. You can go ahead and reserve a username through Proton Mail for them, and they have 15 years to activate it. Once they're old enough, they'll already have a private email set up. Choose an address and pay $1 toward the Proton Foundation, then save the voucher to share with your child down the line.

If you're moving to Proton Mail from a different email provider or simply want all of your messages in one inbox, you can use Proton's Easy Switch feature to connect with and import from Gmail, Yahoo Mail, Outlook, and any other provider that allows IMAP access. Once Easy Switch is on, you'll be able to receive and send messages from your external address within Proton, and any mail sent to another Proton user from that address will be end-to-end encrypted. You'll retain copies of messages in your external inbox, so you don't need to make the full transition immediately. Easy Switch can also migrate your contacts and calendars. Go to Settings > Import via Easy Switch, choose your email service, and follow the prompts.

We've all sent emails we wish we could take back thanks to a typo we didn't notice, an attachment we forgot to add, or a message we regret. Proton Mail has a delayed send feature that gives you up to 20 seconds to change your mind before your email is out of your hands. The timer is set at 10 seconds by default, but you can adjust it down to 0 or 5 seconds or up to 20. Go to Settings > Messages and composing, scroll down to the Composing section, and choose your desired time from the Undo send dropdown.

There are plenty of good reasons to use an email alias, from keeping your primary address private to easily filtering messages from mailing lists. Proton Mail supports unlimited plus addressing, meaning you can simply add a plus symbol and word after your username to create a new email—such as [username][email protected]—and receive messages in your regular inbox (with filters if you set them up). This can be done when you Alternatively, you can create a randomly generated email alias, which keeps your username hidden. Free users get up to 10, while paid subscribers can create unlimited aliases. On the web interface, click the security shield icon, go to Hide-my-email aliases, and click New alias.

Messages between Proton users are automatically encrypted end to end, but if your recipient doesn't use Proton Mail, you can set up a password for your emails to keep them private. Replies to password-protected emails are also encrypted (though your reply to that reply will require you to re-enable encryption). When you compose your message, click the padlock icon in the bottom toolbar and enter a password and password hint. You can set an expiration date as well. Note that you'll need to share the password with the recipient separately.

Another Proton Mail security feature is the expiration timer, which will auto-delete emails you send and receive after a set period, preventing messages from hanging around in inboxes and sent folders indefinitely. Messages that you send to other Proton Mail users as well as password-protected emails to those outside of Proton can be set to expire. If you have a paid account, you can also set emails you receive to self-destruct (in addition to auto-delete for messages in trash). Click the hourglass icon at the bottom of the message and set the expiration date and time. If you are sending a password-protected email to a non-Proton user, check the box. Then hit Set.

When you take a photo, image metadata may reveal locations, times and dates, and other information that can be used to track you if it falls into the wrong hands. Proton Mail can strip that out for sent images, so you can share photos via email without giving any unnecessary data away. When you attach an image to an email draft, choose Remove metadata when prompted.

Because of Proton's encryption, the standard search feature reads only names, dates, email addresses, and subject lines. If you want to include message content, you'll need to enable the feature that builds a local index in your browser, protecting it from intrusion unless someone has physical access to your device. Click the search bar at the top of your inbox on the web app and tap Enable next to Search message content. Click Enable to confirm. Note that indexing does require storage space, but once complete, it'll automatically update as long as your browser is open.

title: Judge clears a lawsuit against Kyrsten Sinema under North Carolina's 'homewrecker' law
description: Former U.S. Sen. Kyrsten Sinema can be sued under North Carolina's homewrecker law over her relationship with a member of her security detail, a judge ruled Friday.  Sinema has acknowledged having a r...
fullText:
PHOENIX (AP) — Former U.S. Sen. Kyrsten Sinema can be sued under North Carolina's homewrecker law over her relationship with a member of her security detail, a judge ruled Friday.

Sinema has acknowledged having a romantic relationship with Matthew Ammel but argued that she can't be sued in North Carolina because she has no connection to the state.

U.S. District Judge David A. Bragdon rejected that argument, saying nine text messages she sent Ammel while he was in the state give North Carolina jurisdiction over her. He found it implausible that she was unaware of Ammel's whereabouts when she texted him.

Sinema's lawyer, Steven Epstein, did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment.

The lawsuit, filed by Ammel's ex-wife, seeks financial damages from Sinema, who represented Arizona in the U.S. House and later the Senate for one term that ended early last year. North Carolina is one of a handful of states that allow jilted spouses to sue for "alienation of affection" to seek compensation from a third party responsible for the breakup of their marriage.

Matthew and Heather Ammel had "a good and loving marriage" with "genuine love and affection" before Sinema interfered, pursuing Matthew Ammel despite knowing he was married, Heather Ammel alleges in her lawsuit.

Matthew Ammel joined Sinema's security team after he retired from the Army in 2022 and accompanied her on domestic and foreign travel, according to Heather Ammel's complaint.

In early 2024, Heather Ammel discovered "romantic and lascivious" messages her husband had exchanged with Sinema over the Signal messaging app. That summer, he stopped wearing his wedding ring and Sinema gave him a job as a national security fellow in her Senate office while he continued to work for her campaign as a bodyguard, the lawsuit alleges.

Sinema described their sexual encounters during a deposition in July. She said the relationship turned sexual on May 27, 2024, during a trip to Napa, California. She said they later had sexual encounters in New York, Washington, Colorado and Arizona, but never North Carolina.

Matthew and Heather Ammel separated on Nov. 1, 2024.

title: 'My position now is as one of two 10s' - Kane breaks down his evolution
description: Harry Kane was the highest goalscorer in Europe last season, yet he plays like a midfielder. We ask him to break down his game.
fullText:
As Harry Kane's career has progressed, the 33-year-old has taken an increasingly complete role, popping up to collect the ball as deep as his own box.

Many wonder why a talisman tasked with scoring doesn't spend more time closer to goal, but last season the England and Bayern Munich striker scored 73 goals - the highest tally of his career - while playing deeper than he ever has done.

When I mention this paradox, a grin spreads across his face.

"Until you really understand football and understand what we've been talking about, it's so easy to say 'stay high, you're going to score' but it doesn't work like that," Kane says.

I sat down to speak to Kane about the finer details of his game, shedding light on his unique role.

Watching Kane train, his professionalism is palpable. England's record goalscorer is one of the first out on the pitch. The younger players indulge in playful kick-ups as he watches, engaged in conversation with a member of staff.

From a distance, that makes it easy to confuse him with a coach but, given his role on the pitch, it is a fitting mistake.

Kane's style of play reflects who he is as a person, with those who know him saying he is well-rounded and humble on and off the pitch.

The season is in its infancy but Kane isn't basking in the success of the past 12 months. With only five days of pre-season training under his belt, the England captain completed 90 minutes of Bayern's 2-1 win over Borussia Dortmund to lift the German Super Cup.

As demanding as his roaming role is, he has taken the physical demands of it in his stride. Across the past six seasons, STATSports - a sports technology company Kane has invested in - found his distance covered, high-speed running and accelerations were up 8%, 22% and 42% respectively.

And given how the tactical landscape has changed over that time, it is particularly impressive Kane has been able to not only keep up, but stay ahead.

"Over the last five or six years, man-to-man pressure has become bigger," Kane says.

"European football is physical and top teams are trying to win the ball back high, trusting their defenders and midfielders to defend man for man to win their battles."

Given that change, the best teams have recruited physical athletes and brilliant dribblers who can beat their man when the game becomes a series of one-against-ones.

Kane, not known for his dribbling - and by his own admission "not the fastest", has thrived on his own terms.

Against Dortmund, there was a specific moment Kane dropped deep, looking to arrive in space unmarked. Recognising the danger, two players converged on the Englishman.

Kane's dribbling is cerebral. His speed of thought provides him solutions to problems others would attempt to solve with their feet alone.

After getting low and using his strength to shrug centre-back Waldemar Anton off him, Kane rose, slightly adjusting his body to the right. These micro-adjustments are a hallmark of his game and through them he is able to shift an entire team's momentum.

Fooled by this feint, Daniel Svensson and Jobe Bellingham found themselves wrong-footed as Kane snapped the ball back the other way, opening up the entire pitch from within Bayern's half.

Earlier this year, Bayern boss Vincent Kompany shed light on Kane's unique role, explaining it as being 50% coached and 50% Kane deciding what to do.

"I think it's partly instinct, using my football brain and getting the feeling on the pitch," says Kane. "If, for example, I want to drop and see if the centre-back really wants to commit, he might commit into midfield, but is he going to commit if I drop all the way to my box?

"After the first five or 10 minutes you really get an understanding of how the opposition are going to play, which dictates how I play."

There is a shared understanding at Bayern of an approach that allows team-mates to make sense of rotations that, to the naked eye, appear random.

Kane, who is given more freedom than most, is at the centre of it.

"I feel like my position now is as one of two 10s, and you work together," he says. "You can double up on one side to overload, which causes the opposition centre-backs a problem of who to mark.

"If they want to mark both, they've got to go man-to-man and then that leaves space for our wingers or full-backs to run into.

"It's posing all these questions to the opposition but, personally, I love having someone close to me who I can link with."

Kane built his reputation playing as a lone number nine, so it is interesting to hear him identify instead as a number 10 - in a front two.

"When you're the number nine on your own you can get marked by two centre-backs and you struggle to get touches on the ball," he says. "You're relying on everyone else to find you with the ball."

Showing Kane two clips from last season, I ask him to talk through what was going through his head.

"The thing with our formation is, as long as there's someone in each position, it doesn't really matter who it is. Lucho [Luis Diaz] in this clip is playing as one of those 10s.

"I've come off to try and create a bit of space and Lucho's gone through the centre."

Distracted by Kane's dropping-deep movement, one of the opposition midfielders is pulled towards him. This creates space, allowing Joshua Kimmich to punch the ball through to Diaz.

"I think it's Serge [Gnabry] making the run in behind which takes the defenders back, which allows me and Lucho that space in between. Lucho lays it off and whenever I'm in that position, around 20-25 yards out, I'm always looking if I can get my shot off."

It is one of many examples of Kane initially dropping deep before scoring.

"By playing deep when the play develops, I end up coming into a number 10 spot when everyone's dropped," he says. "I can get shots off from the edge of the box, which is a big strength of mine, or I'm running off the back of players where no-one's picking me up - because the midfielder finds it hard to [track]."

The second clip is from Bayern's Champions League tie against Club Brugge.

Usually Kane is marked by an opposition centre-back, but the Belgian club give that responsibility to their holding midfielder - something he recognises and exploits.

Lennart Karl scores without Kane touching the ball, but the striker's involvement is undeniable.

"These are the little runs, again, not everyone sees," Kane explains. "With Jamal Musiala and Lenny, they're so good at receiving the ball and dribbling so there'll be times where I will actually stay higher and let those guys get on the ball a bit deeper, and I'll try and make runs in behind.

"Without changing my game too much, I try and complement the players around me.

"I know Lenny is so good in those pockets and when he gets there, I'm more thinking of running in behind because, one, he can play me in and I can go through on goal, or two, he can dribble with the ball and do exactly what happened here.

"As soon as Lenny gets in that pocket I make the run and not always to get the ball, sometimes it is just to drag the defender away.

"Now he's one-against-one with a centre-back in the middle of the pitch and that's dangerous for any centre-back."

With the Ballon d'Or announcement on the horizon, Kane's name is in the conversation, primarily for the sheer volume of goals he has scored. What is easier to miss in that debate is the rest of his game.

Kane plays for the team in each phase of the game across the entirety of the pitch, while at the same time producing extraordinary individual numbers that match the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Erling Haaland.

He has described himself as playing in the role of a number 10, nine and six at times.

In a football world of specific and heavily drilled tactical roles, that is quite the achievement.

title: SFA propose youth quotas along with financial incentives
description: The Scottish FA is proposing financial incentives - and penalties - in a bid to get more homegrown talent playing, with clubs to vote on three initiatives aimed at increased game-time for under-21s.
fullText:
The Scottish FA is proposing financial incentives - and penalties - along with quotas, in a bid to get more homegrown talent playing for clubs.

The governing body has put forward three suggestions to increase game time for young Scottish players, which will be voted on at a SFA general meeting in October and the SPFL's agm in November.

Two under-21 Scotland-eligible players start in all Scottish Cup matches, with one player on the pitch at all times.

Two under-21 Scotland-eligible players start in all Premier Sports Cup matches, with one player on the pitch at all times.

Under-21 Scotland-eligible players in all four SPFL divisions to play an average of 60 minutes per game, across the season, (6% of available minutes).

If approved, the regulations would commence from the 2027-2028 season.

All 42 SPFL clubs gathered in St Andrews on Friday to discuss improving pathways for young talent and finding the next generation of international players.

The SFA say an extra £1m would be made available to clubs.

Under the league recommendation, clubs failing to reach the target of 60 minutes per game would be deducted 10% of their final-placing prize money, with those funds redistributed among those who achieve it.

The proposals come as figures show a dramatic dip in Scottish-born players being fielded by top-flight clubs and suggestions of a fear by managers and owners to take a chance on academy players.

Statistics also reflect a huge increase in young players being tempted south to club academies in England, prompting concerns they could be lost in a vast youth system rather than breaking into first teams north of the border.

Club owners watched a presentation by football analytics company Twenty First Group, who outlined data showing the financial incentives of fielding and developing academy players.

Twenty First Group say that, compared to similar sized nations, Scottish clubs are collectively missing out on £40m annually by not playing younger players and selling them on.

Club Brugge recruitment director Guilian Preud'homme also delivered a presentation about the success enjoyed by the Belgian champions after they shifted their focus from overseas recruitment to homegrown talent.

Scotland has slipped to 18th in Uefa's coefficient, with under-21 Scottish eligible players amassing 18,706 minutes in the top flight last year, compared to 80,345 minutes in 2013.

That was the year rules requiring Scottish top flight clubs to have three outfield players under 21 in their matchday squad of 18 were abolished.

"Scotland's return to the World Cup created a huge sense of excitement around the national team, but it has also underlined the need to plan for the next generation," said SFA chief executive Ian Maxwell.

"Clubs across Europe are showing that giving younger players minutes does not have to come at the expense of success on the pitch, and we believe that these proposals could both strengthen Scottish clubs and have a positive effect on the national team in the future."

SFA chief football officer Craig Mulholland pointed to the gains made since last year's introduction of a co-operation system and the revamp of the KDM Evolution Trophy but said the "lack of opportunities in the top flight is concerning".

Mulholland added: "We're at a point where we need to take a holistic approach to improvement.

"The time for reviews is over: it's time for action to make sure that our young Scottish people get the best opportunity to go and become top professionals.

"We would always love to do more but we believe that introducing requirements for under-21 players in the Scottish Cup and League Cup and targets for minutes in the Premiership would represent a significant step."

title: Trump thrashes Zhao to reach last four of British Open
description: Judd Trump thrashes world number one Zhao Xintong 5-1 as he moves into the semi-finals of the British Open.
fullText:
Judd Trump thrashed world number one Zhao Xintong 5-1 as he moved into the semi-finals of the British Open.

The Englishman will now face Aaron Hill or Jak Jones on Saturday, with Mark Selby taking on Liam Highfield in the other last-four encounter.

"When it goes down to two or one table it is a completely different set-up and you feel like the tournament comes alive," Trump said on Channel 5.

"In that kind of scenario I am so used to being out there and it gets the adrenalin going and it gets me more up for the fight especially against him [Zhao].

Earlier on Friday, Highfield had defeated teenage star Stan Moody 5-2, while Selby claimed a thumping 5-0 victory over Jack Lisowski.

And Trump delivered more of the same in the evening against the man who recently deposed him at the top of the rankings.

The 37-year-old, who has won 31 ranking titles, opened with a break of 101 and 57 to take the opening two frames before Zhao responded with a century of his own.

However, Trump restricted his Chinese opponent to just 29 points over the following three frames, while knocking in two further half-centuries to easily advance.

"[I was] probably a little more determined than normal," Trump added.

"In the past when I have lost the number one spot or people put other players as the favourite, you don't have that as number one and have that same demeanour of wanting to prove everyone wrong or that I'm the best."

title: Hull KR secure top-six place with win over Giants
description: Reigning Super League champions Hull KR make sure of their place in this season's play-offs with a dominant win over Huddersfield Giants.
fullText:
Tries: Minchella, Mourgue 2, Broadbent, Litten, Davies Goals: Mourgue 3, Martin 3

Hull Kingston Rovers secured their place in the Super League play-offs with an early try glut against Huddersfield Giants.

The reigning Super League champions went into the home game against the in-form Giants off the back of three straight defeats, but restored several of their front-line players to the team after resting them in last week's heavy defeat by Wigan Warriors.

In what was head coach Willie Peters' final home game before he leaves to take charge of new franchise PNG Chiefs in the NRL, the Robins took control as captain Elliot Minchella, Arthur Mourgue and Jack Broadbent scored tries in the opening 17 minutes.

The Giants, who had hauled themselves up from being adrift at the bottom with five wins from their previous six games, hit back through Tanguy Zenon but tries from Jez Litten, Mourgue and Tom Davies secured Rovers' place in the play-offs.

Leigh seal top-six spot to end Saints' play-off bid

Hull FC fightback not enough to overhaul Toulouse

Peters has taken the Robins to new heights during his four years at the club, culminating in last season's domestic treble and victory in the World Club Challenge earlier this year.

After the match, he said his farewells to home fans, with a top-four place now out of reach.

His team, which has been underwhelming at times this season, showed some of their championship class with three tries in the space of eight minutes to dispel any nerves against a Giants side which put a temporary dent in Leigh Leopards' play-off push last week.

The excellent Minchella finished a spell of severe pressure on the Huddersfield line with a powerful finish, Mourgue side-stepped past two tackles for another and Broadbent raced over from Peta Hiku's pass.

Zenon's try late in the half revived a few doubts but they were quickly quelled as the reliable Rhyse Martin, also making his final home appearance before following Peters to PNG, kicked a penalty and Litten's opportunist finish opened the gap to 20 points.

Minchella, one of seven big guns restored to the side, unselfishly set up Mourgue for his second try of the night and Davies' finish in the corner wrapped up a comfortable win which, together with St Helens' defeat, means the Robins' defence of their title will continue into the play-offs.

title: US issues sanctions on Turkish bank that it calls a 'critical financial lifeline' for Iran
description: The Trump administration announced Friday that it has imposed sanctions on a Turkish financial institution as part of its latest effort to sever “critical financial lifelines” for the Iranian governme...
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration announced Friday that it has imposed sanctions on a Turkish financial institution as part of its latest effort to sever "critical financial lifelines" for the Iranian government.

The actions against Golden Global Yatirim Bankasi Anonim Sirketi come after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent last week launched "Operation Economic Outcast, " Washington's new effort to isolate already heavily sanctioned Iran from its remaining trading partners to try to get it to capitulate to U.S. demands after more than six months of war.

The Treasury Department accused the Turkish bank and its entities of being established to enable Iran's efforts to transfer oil revenues from China to Turkey, where they could then be converted to cash and gold. It also said the institution "knowingly offered" banking services to Iranian financial entities, including those already sanctioned by the U.S. government in 2022 for funneling Tehran's oil sales.

Bessent, who had told The Associated Press earlier this week that another bank would face economic penalties, said financial institutions with ties to Iran will "continue to find out the hard way that we are serious about Operation Economic Outcast."

"While we hope no more banks will need to be sanctioned, that ultimately depends on how quickly the international community comes to its senses and ceases support of the murderous Iranian regime," he said in a press release Friday. "We know who you are, we know where you are, and we will continue to take action together with our allies and partners until we have buried the head of the Iranian snake."

But so far, the goal to force those that still do business with Iran to cut off financial ties or face U.S. retaliation has fallen flat, with promises of an "economic D-Day" for a group of countries that could include China and India quickly turning into warnings and negotiations with Iran's trading partners.

Bessent had previously told reporters that he wanted countries to have an opportunity to shift away from Iran before it was too late in a bid to avoid upending the global financial system.

The Trump administration's reluctance to penalize major trading partners that still do business with Iran was on display last week when the U.S. took steps to limit an Egyptian bank's operations in the United Arab Emirates but stopped short of imposing sanctions.

The U.S. also has resumed military strikes in recent days, prompting Iranian retaliation in the region. It's unclear what the outcome of the two-pronged strategy will be for President Donald Trump, who has struggled to end an unpopular war with an intransigent Iranian government as energy prices rise and pose problems for Republicans before November's midterm congressional elections.

Targeted in the latest U.S. sanctions is Golden Global Investment Bank, which was founded in 2019 as Turkey's first investment bank to offer "banking services and alternative financing methods" to foreign companies, according to its website.

The Istanbul-based bank, which is largely unfamiliar to most Turks, says it aims to increase Turkey's foreign trade through target markets in neighboring countries.

The Treasury announcement came a day after Turkey's state-run Halkbank declared it had reached a settlement with the U.S. Justice Department in a nine-year case focused on violating sanctions with Iran.

In that case, senior officials at Halkbank were said to have illegally moved about $20 billion worth of Iranian oil revenues. U.S. prosecutors claimed high-ranking Turkish government officials received millions of dollars in bribes to protect the scheme.

The Halkbank case caused a rift in U.S.-Turkey relations, with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan personally lobbying the White House to have the case dropped.

title: FA to canvass England players in World Cup review
description: The Football Association's review into England's World Cup campaign will canvass the opinions of players involved in the tournament.
fullText:
The Football Association's review into England's World Cup campaign will canvass the opinions of players involved in the tournament.

English football's governing body has started the post-tournament review they conduct after every major international competition. The FA says the review is the standard process it undertakes after all tournaments.

Head coach Thomas Tuchel and members of his backroom team were at St George's Park last week where they were involved in unpacking their performance in north America with a wider report into the team's World Cup campaign to be delivered at a later date.

And it is understood members of Tuchel's squad will be spoken to, and their feedback taken into account, as part of the review process.

The players' involvement in the review provides an interesting dynamic given the emerging sense from members of the World Cup squad that Tuchel's substitutions and tactical approach contributed to their semi-final loss to Argentina - despite taking a 1-0 lead through Anthony Gordon.

BBC Sport revealed in the 24 hours after that defeat that at least three senior players privately expressed misgivings about Tuchel's approach in the closing stages of the game.

There was a widely held view that Tuchel's changes and tactical set-up were too defensive late on as they conceded two late goals to lose 2-1.

The ongoing review will also look into the impact of the team's permanent Kansas City base during the tournament.

After every game, they returned to Kansas City - and the effects of the travelling will be analysed.

England went on to defeat France in the bronze medal match to record their best World Cup finish since lifting the trophy in 1966.

With that in mind, key figures at the FA view the tournament as a success and the organisation has backed Tuchel before the Euro 2028 qualifying campaign.

England will play their first game since the World Cup in the Nations League against Spain on 26 September. They will also face two matches in the tournament against the Czech Republic, either side of playing Croatia, during the next international window.

title: Leigh seal top-six spot as St Helens fail to make play-offs
description: Leigh Leopards secure a Super League top-six finish by thrashing St Helens, ending Saints' hopes of reaching the play-offs.
fullText:
Tries: Charnley, Armstrong, Hanley 2, Cook, Ipape, Alick-Wiencke, Mulhern Goals: Cook 8

Tries: Douglas, Sailor Goal: Sailor

Leigh Leopards secured their place in Super League's top six by thrashing St Helens, who will now not appear in the play-offs for the first time in the Super League era.

Saints' hopes of protecting their unblemished record were ended by an ignominious defeat as Leigh ran in eight tries.

Tries from Josh Charnley, David Armstrong, Umyla Hanley and Adam Cook opened up a 24-10 half-time lead, with Jacob Douglas and Tristan Sailor replying for Saints.

After half-time, Mark Percival was sin-binned for Saints before Edwin Ipape extended Leigh's lead, Hanley scored his second try and Jacob Alick-Wiencke and Robbie Mulhern also crossed.

Hull KR secure top-six place with win over Giants

Hull FC fightback not enough to overhaul Toulouse

Victory secured Leigh's place in the play-offs for the fourth consecutive season and kept them fifth in the table. They could yet move up to fourth, above Wakefield, after next week's final round of fixtures.

It took them 10 minutes to score the first try as Saints failed to deal with Cook's kick, which fell for Leigh to spread the ball for Charnley to walk in on the right wing.

He then celebrated by signing a mock contract and, moments later, the public address confirmed he had signed a new deal for the 2027 season.

Leigh scored a second try four minutes later as Armstrong, Cook and Lachlan Lam combined from deep in their own half to break up the left before Armstrong sprinted in from halfway.

Saints responded by working space for Douglas to go over in the right corner before phenomenal feet from Harry Robertson left the defence for dead and he sent Sailor under the posts.

But Robertson then missed a tackle that allowed Innes Senior to break for Leigh and create Hanley's first try, before Ipape drove for the line, his offload went to ground but Cook grubbered in-goal and touched down.

After half-time, St Helens blew a two-on-one on the left wing before they lost Percival - who recently announced he will retire at the end of the season - to the sin bin for a high tackle.

Leigh eventually made the extra man count when a second set of six and a quick play-the-ball under the posts led to Ipape barging over.

Shane Wright then gave a penalty away for obstruction in the shadow of his own posts and Leigh worked the ball to Hanley on the right, who burst through three tackles to find the line.

Further tries in the rain would follow as Alick-Wiencke slid in before Mulhern charged over with the final play of the game.

Leigh Leopards head coach Adrian Lam told BBC Radio Manchester:

"We wanted to respond from last week and I'm pleased, it puts us back on track.

"Josh [Charnley] is still playing as well as he has been, he's a fan favourite and a big part of this club. The legacy and DNA we've been building since we came back up - he's been a big part of that.

"Had you had said to us a quarter of the way through [the season], would you accept where we are now? Absolutely."

St Helens interim head coach Eamon O'Carroll told BBC Radio Merseyside:

"The scoreline probably doesn't reflect the effort and I'm unbelievably proud of the players.

"I've been in this role for six weeks and if there's one thing I wanted to get out of it, it is that we had a team that turned up for each other and we had that tonight.

"It's great to give young lads a chance, ideally you'd like to do it with a few more senior players around them, so they're not exposed as much, but they can hold their heads up and they'll certainly be better for this experience."

title: Improving Alcaraz underlines title credentials in wide-open draw
description: Defending champion Carlos Alcaraz underlines his US Open title credentials by sweeping aside Wu Yibing to reach the fourth round as the draw opens up further.
fullText:
Carlos Alcaraz swept Wu Yibing aside to reach the US Open fourth round - and said he is getting better with every match as he continues his return from a long-term injury lay-off.

The Spaniard underlined why he remains a serious contender to defend his title in New York with a 6-3 6-4 6-1 victory over China's Wu.

The 23-year-old's opening-round match in Flushing Meadows was his first on a singles court for 139 days after injuring his wrist in April.

Alcaraz came through his opener in straight sets but had to battle back from a set down against Portugal's Jaime Faria in the second round.

However, Alcaraz continued to build momentum on Friday, needing two hours and 20 minutes on court to beat Wu.

"To be honest, I'm better than I thought," the seven-time major champion said.

"Physically I thought I was going to be bad after the first match, but I am recovering really well. I am doing great things off the court to be in a good state.

"Right now, I think my level is really good. I think I have caught the rhythm of the competition.

"Every time that I step on the court I give it all. I'm just trying to improve, be better every match and I think I'm getting there."

American 20th seed Tommy Paul - who Alcaraz has beaten six times in a row - awaits in the fourth round.

Alcaraz's path to an eighth major title has opened up over the past few days.

French Open champion and Wimbledon runner-up Alexander Zverev heads the men's draw in the absence of injured world number one Jannik Sinner.

As the second seed, Alcaraz cannot meet Zverev until the final - and the German has been taken to five sets and kept on court until 2am in his two matches so far.

Novak Djokovic suffered a shock first-round exit to Argentine Mariano Navone, while Canadian third seed Felix Auger-Aliassime lost to Karen Khachanov in the second round.

As it stands, American eighth seed Ben Shelton is the only top-10 player that Alcaraz can meet before the semi-finals. He could then face seventh seed Daniil Medvedev in the last four.

Alcaraz has won all three of his meetings with Shelton and has a 6-3 winning head-to-head against Medvedev - although the inconsistent Russian beat him at Indian Wells in March.

Meanwhile, Zverev's potential pre-final opponents include home hope Taylor Fritz and Italy's French Open runner-up Flavio Cobolli.

'It's so strong' - Sabalenka halts play over cannabis smell

100 influencers invited to US Open spark debate on 'tennis etiquette'

While Alcaraz at times appeared frustrated with his own inconsistency against Wu, the former world number three continues to demonstrate progress.

Alcaraz landed 21 winners as he extended his career-best streak of Grand Slam singles match wins to 17, but that was counteracted by 33 unforced errors and a first-serve success rate of just 67%.

Despite a seemingly straightforward scoreline, Alcaraz did not have it all his own way and repeatedly made his feelings clear on the court.

He surrendered early advantages in the first two sets - his first serve dipped to 53% in the second set - but managed to reset to avoid further complications.

"Every win Alcaraz gets, he is becoming more of a favourite," former Wimbledon champion Pat Cash said on BBC Radio 5 Live.

"Four months off, no matches and win the US Open? He is a class above everybody else, when he is good, and he is getting better by the moment.

"The way he is moving, there is no reason for him not to do well."

Former champion Medvedev also progressed on Friday, overcoming French 26th seed Arthur Rinderknech 6-4 6-4 6-4.

Medvedev achieved his sole major title at the US Open in 2021, and has won 21 of his 23 singles titles on hard courts.

He appears in the form to challenge again, on the evidence of his three straight-set victories so far, but will have to overcome American 11th seed Frances Tiafoe or Monaco's 22nd seed Valentin Vacherot next.

Britons Henry Patten and Joe Salisbury both won their men's doubles first-round matches.

Top seeds Patten and Finnish parner Harri Heliovaara won 6-4 6-2 against Argentine brothers Francisco and Juan Manuel Cerundolo, while Salisbury and American Rajeev Ram beat Australian John-Patrick Smith and Mexico's Santiago Gonzalez 7-6 (7-3) 7-6 (8-6).

Jan Choinski and Bulgaria's Alexander Donski also advanced with a 7-6 (7-5) 6-4 win over American pair Martin Damm and Mackenzie McDonald.

title: Greaves becomes first woman to win match on European Tour
description: Beau Greaves makes darts history by beating Daryl Gurney at the Czech Open to become the first woman to win a match on the European Tour.
fullText:
Beau Greaves made darts history by becoming the first woman to win a match on the European Tour.

The 22-year-old, who was edged out 6-5 by Rob Cross on her European Tour debut in Hungary last week, beat Daryl Gurney 6-4 in the Czech Open.

Gurney beat Greaves in a deciding set in their first-round match at the PDC World Championship in December and he moved into a 3-1 lead in Prague.

However, Greaves reeled off three straight legs with 14, 13 and 11-dart finishes to go 4-3 in front and, even though Gurney levelled at 4-4, she went on to take victory and become the first female winner in the European Tour's 15-year history.

"It feels amazing," said Greaves, who will play world number two Luke Humphries in the second round on Saturday.

"It's just so nice to win a game, I was so nervous at the start, I don't know why. It took me so long to get settled, but luckily I did enough to win the game.

"It means loads to me, the crowd's fantastic. It's such a tight stage and you feel so much from the crowd. I'm really enjoying it and loving the experience."

It is the latest in a list of achievements for Doncaster's Greaves which include her becoming the first woman to win a PDC ranking title when she beat Michael Smith in April.

She is also the first woman to hit a nine-dart finish on the PDC ProTour, having done so in a win against Mensur Suljovic in February.

Greaves also won the Women's World Matchplay for the third time when she beat Fallon Sherrock in July.

On facing Humphries, she added: "I've played Luke on the big stage before so I know what to expect, he's world class so I'm going to have to play a lot better than I did tonight.

"What more do you want than on a Euro Tour to play one of the best players in the world? I'll look forward to it and I'll be ready."

title: Trump administration warms to Zambia despite crackdown worries
description: Washington Democrats said they’re alarmed about post-election violence.
fullText:
The Trump administration is warming to Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema following his disputed reelection despite growing concerns in Washington about a post-election crackdown.

US Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs Frank Garcia attended Hichilema's inauguration this week during his second trip to the continent in the role. He also met separately with the Zambian leader. Hichilema said Zambia looks "forward to further strengthening our bilateral relations" with the US.

A State Department spokesperson told Semafor that the trip was a continuation of a decades-old relationship. "After 62 years of diplomatic relations, the United States remains committed to Zambia's success. We look forward to working with Zambia's government, private sector, and people to deepen a partnership that delivers tangible and enduring benefits for both countries," the spokesperson said.

The Trump administration's posture towards the government in Lusaka contrasts with warnings from Democrats on Capitol Hill, some of whom had urged the State Department before the August 13 vote to press for a free and fair election.

Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, D-N.H., the top Democrat on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, told Semafor that "democratic backsliding in Zambia is a major concern for the Southern African region," adding that post-election "violence and arbitrary arrest" are signs of "a clear divergence from Zambia's legacy of competitive elections and peaceful transfers of power." She called on Hichilema and his party to move forward with reforms because "clear violations of democratic gains threaten not only the safety and security of Zambians but also the positive relationship the US has built with the Hichilema administration."

Rep. Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, urged Secretary of State Marco Rubio to "call on President Hichilema to release the electoral results from Zambia's polling stations, investigate the fatal shooting of former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya, and allow the courts to hear legal challenges." He cited the need for a "firm response" ahead of upcoming elections in Angola, Kenya, and Nigeria. Kafwaya was killed during a police raid on a house occupied by opposition leaders following the August election.

Senate Africa subcommittee ranking member Cory Booker, D-N.J., called the killing of Kafwaya and the arrests of opposition members "deeply concerning."

A representative for Senate Foreign Relations Committee Chairman Jim Risch, R-Idaho, declined to comment. Other Republican lawmakers working on Africa policy did not return requests for comment by press time.

Zambia's election commission declared Hichilema the winner on August 18 with about 60% of the vote against opposition candidate Brian Mundubile's roughly 38%. Mundubile has alleged irregularities and election observers have also reported inflated vote tallies and improper administration. Authorities sealed off the courts on the final day to file an election petition, clearing the way for Hichilema's inauguration.

Post-election crackdowns left Mundubile and many of his allies facing treason charges that a UN human rights official called "concocted."

Zambia is central to the US-backed Lobito Corridor linking Angola, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and Zambia's copper belt to the Atlantic. But ties between the US and Zambia frayed this year following reports the State Department was tying health funding to preferential mineral access for US firms, a plan that Zambia rejected.

title: Isak finally arrives as Gakpo proves value to Liverpool
description: Has the real Alexander Isak finally arrived at Liverpool after his two-goal display in their Premier League win at Ipswich Town, asks chief football writer Phil McNulty?
fullText:
Alexander Isak was the £125m striker who finally arrived at Liverpool by tormenting Ipswich Town - while Cody Gakpo's virtuoso performance had them giving thanks he never left.

The nuts and bolts of a comfortable Friday in Suffolk were that Liverpool won 2-0 - thanks to two Isak goals in the first nine minutes, giving them their first Premier League victory of the season and new manager Andoni Iraola's first since succeeding the sacked Arne Slot.

Liverpool's win must be placed in the context of being against a newly promoted Ipswich Town who were game, but who shipped five goals at Manchester United last week and look ripe for the picking against attacking quality.

The wider significance, however, was that Isak finally looked like the player Liverpool broke, at that time, the British transfer record to seal an acrimonious transfer from Newcastle United last summer.

Throw in the added bonus that Bradley Barcola showed flashes of devastating pace in a 26-minute debut display after his £123m arrival from Paris St-Germain, and this was a night that ticked every box for Iraola and Liverpool.

Even Barcola's bow, however, was overshadowed by Isak.

The Sweden striker looked a lost soul in his first season at Liverpool, arriving out of condition after downing tools to secure his move from Tyneside, then troubled by injuries as he gave the impression of being the most expensive vanity purchase in British football history.

He was outshone by fellow striker Hugo Ekitike, his statistics stark as he suffered along with many others in an astonishing decline amid Liverpool's dismal title defence that led to Slot's sacking only a year after he lifted the Premier League trophy.

Isak played 22 games encompassing 1,033 minutes, scoring four goals at a rate of one every 258 minutes. He played 14 games in the Premier League totalling 703 minutes, scoring only three goals at a rate of one every 234 minutes.

He has already equalled that league tally this season, but it was his demeanour as well as his lethal finishing that will have given Liverpool and Iraola confidence that the Isak code has finally been cracked.

And it was done by utilising Isak at his best - running in behind defenders and pressing with pace. It was what made him such a hot property at Newcastle United, and made everything about his every miserable moment on the pitch with Liverpool last term such a mystery.

It was also done in tandem with Gakpo, who could easily have been back in the north west preparing for Manchester City's game against Coventry City at Etihad Stadium had the move not collapsed.

Isak shines at last but Scherpen suffers - Ipswich v Liverpool player ratings

Gakpo was happy to join Enzo Maresca's Manchester City transition, but Liverpool's failure to sign Yankuba Minteh from Brighton or Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr meant he stayed at Anfield.

And it might just be one of those twists of fate football can throw up as Gakpo delivered a masterclass of creation that meant this game was effectively over after nine minutes.

Isak was the spearhead who delivered the defining moments, starting in the sixth minute when he took Gakpo's clever pass between Leif Davis and Jacob Greaves before thrashing a right-foot shot that carried too much power for Ipswich Town keeper Kjell Scherpen, although he had to do much, much better than divert the striker's effort into the net.

The second, three minutes later, was stamped right through with class, bringing a beaming smile to the face of Iraola.

Gakpo delivered a delicious pass with the outside of his right foot from inside his own half. Isak used a left-foot flick to move inside Greaves as Scherpen came out, before a touch with his right foot sent the Ipswich keeper the wrong way before rolling in a cool finish with his left.

Perfection from Gakpo's start to Isak's finish. Game over.

Isak had a desperately poor return to Tyneside on the opening day of the season, questions even coming about his performance after he scored in Liverpool's 2-2 draw at home to Nottingham Forest in their second game.

This, however, was Isak played right - and playing right.

Iraola said: "He's a massive player for us. My demands will probably not be about the goals. I know he is fit and in good shape. He's going to produce the numbers.

"My fight with him will be more about other stuff, how to help the team in other situations - but it is good he has already played two full games, scoring the goals, so I am very happy to have him."

And Isak added: "We were waiting for the first win. We talked about starting the game good, which we haven't done recently, so it was perfect for us to get two good quick goals.

"With a normal pre-season, I think we are starting to get to the way we want to play. To be offensive and attack the defence. I think we did that. We scored two, and we could have scored more."

Reflecting on his poor first season at Liverpool, Isak said: "It was not easy. It was obviously a long injury and a difficult season in general. I was thinking to have a good World Cup, and then to start off the season well, which I think I have done now. It's kind of behind me, but it wasn't easy."

Portman Road is certainly a happy hunting ground for Isak. Since the start of the 2024-25 season, his five Premier League goals there are the joint most by any player at an away ground, equalling Erling Haaland's haul against Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park.

Gakpo also struggled for his best form in the last campaign, but he has started this season in outstanding style. This was the elegant Netherlands forward at his best, not just by making two goals, but with his all-round performance.

Liverpool captain and compatriot Virgil van Dijk is certainly delighted to still be lining up alongside his team-mate for club and country, saying: "It's massive. I said it before the transfer window had closed.

"He's important for us, and he will be important this season. He showed it here. He showed it last week as well, and over the last couple of years. He needs to just keep going."

The same challenge now applies to Isak. Iraola will not want this to be a false dawn for such an exceptional talent that had lost his way.

title: Kolisi urges Boks to channel spirit of Soweto to beat All Blacks
description: Captain Siya Kolisi calls on the Springboks to summon inspiration from Soweto's pivotal part in South Africa's history as they host New Zealand on Saturday.
fullText:
Captain Siya Kolisi has called on the Springboks to summon inspiration from Soweto's pivotal part in South Africa's history as they take on New Zealand on the edge of the Johannesburg township on Saturday.

The 94,736-capacity FNB Stadium staged the opening match of football's World Cup, the first and only time the tournament has been staged in Africa.

However, Kolisi, South Africa's first black captain, also referenced 1976's Soweto Uprising - the student protests that were a turning point in the fight against apartheid, the state-backed racial segregation of South African society.

"So many things that happened in Soweto helped shape the South Africa we have today," said Kolisi.

"So many heroes have come from there, and a lot of the football history of this country is from Soweto, so we know how special that is.

"We're not going to act like it's not a special ground in a significant area. All of that gives us more to play for. We are also thankful for the people who came from there and fought for people like me and [assistant coach Mzwandile] Stick to be sitting here today.

"They fought for the freedom we have now and never got to experience it, and giving our best tomorrow is part of us saying thank you."

The Soweto Uprising was a protest by school children and students against black schools being ordered to teach in English and Afrikaans, languages mainly used by the country's white population. Hundreds of protestors were killed by police as clashes continued and spread through Johannesburg.

International condemnation of South Africa's government followed. Apartheid ended in 1994 with South Africa's first fully democratic elections.

New Zealand have won their two previous visits to FNB Stadium and another victory would put them 2-1 up in the series - replicating the scoreline from the All Blacks' 'Incomparables' 1996 success on South African soil - before a fourth and final meeting in the American city of Baltimore on 12 September.

The match is being staged as a double-header with the nations' women's teams meeting in a repeat of the Black Ferns' 46-17 victory in the 2025 Women's Rugby World Cup quarter-final.

Both All Black flanker Wallace Sititi and his younger sister Amarante have been named on the replacements' bench for their respective teams, the pair both wearing the number 20 jersey.

If both make it on to the field, they will become the second pair of brother-sister siblings to play for New Zealand on the same day, following Xavier and Annaleah Rush, who took on Australia at Sydney Football Stadium on 29 August 1998.

Wallace and Amarante's father Semo Sititi, who played for Borders and Newcastle and captained Samoa, has travelled to Johannesburg for the match.

"Representing this country is a privilege but doing it alongside my brother is something special. I will always hold it in my heart," said Amarante., external "It's pretty surreal. I'm still buzzing out that I get to be here with my brother but it's really cool and I'm so grateful."

title: Tennessee official says Flock CEO should be hanged 'publicly for treason’ as controversial cameras face revolt
description: Joe Carr called for Flock Safety's CEO to be hanged for treason at a public meeting, igniting a national debate over automated license plate readers.
fullText:
A Tennessee county commissioner is going viral after he told a Flock Safety representative at a public meeting that the company's CEO should be hanged for treason, marking a fever-pitch surrounding personal privacy and open public hostility over the nationwide rollout of the controversial surveillance tools.

"I believe that Flock right now is one of the most hated companies in America. They are one of the most corrupt companies in America," Kingsport Commissioner Joe Carr told a Flock Safety representative at an Aug. 13 work session.

"Quite frankly, sir, I don't think we can make America great again without hanging your CEO publicly for treason," Carr continued. "Your company is an enemy of the American people."

'Darth Vader' Uses Dark Side To Mock Controversial Surveillance Cameras: 'The Emperor Is A Fan Of Flock'

His comments were quickly interrupted by the leader of the commission meeting, who interjected, saying, "Mr. Carr, we are not going to threaten violence to anybody."

Speaking with Fox News Digital, Carr looked to clarify his now-viral remarks.

Flock Safety Cameras Need Constitutional Guardrails Before Further Deployment, Tennessee Mayor Argues

"I didn't call for lynchings, I called for due process," Carr said. "You want to try the guy first, and I don't support political random killings. I definitely don't. But at the same time, you know, the American people are angry. I felt, and I think a lot of them felt, that no elected official was really going hard enough on this. And so I wanted to be the guy to do that."

Carr's criticism comes as Flock's rollout of automated license plate readers draws national scrutiny over government surveillance, data security and personal privacy. Roughly 100 municipalities have canceled or deactivated their contracts with the security company.

Powerful Crime-fighting Surveillance Growth Spurs Lawmakers To Issue Warning: 'Orwellian'

"I think probably the biggest story though isn't really my comments, but people's reaction to them," Carr said. "You can go on any of the posts about it and like 99 percent of the replies are agreeing with me. And I think that's where the American people are at right now."

"People have a right to go about their business without being spied on," he added. "Whether or not they're going to work or going to church, picking their kids up from school, going to football practice or whatever, they have a right to do all these things without being spied on and without having the government logging their every move."

Texas Gov Greg Abbott Moves To Cut State Funding For Ai-powered Flock Cameras Amid Privacy Concerns

Within days of Carr's comments in the work session, Sullivan County Sheriff Jeff Cassidy suspended the use of all 10 of Flock's ALPRs in the county due to "legitimate concerns" surrounding "privacy, oversight, and government surveillance," according to a press release.

Cassidy went on to ask the Sullivan County Commission to consider placing a referendum on the next local ballot "that would allow voters to decide" if the sheriff's office can reinstate the technology.

"I believe the safeguards currently in place within our agency provide clear guidelines for the proper use of this technology. If an employee abuses or misuses the technology, we will take quick and decisive action, up to and including termination or prosecution when warranted," the statement continued.

Despite the sheriff's office's assertion that the cameras had facilitated positive, crime-fighting results within the community — including an instance in which a Flock camera assisted in locating a child predator who had escaped federal custody in a neighboring city — Carr insists their risks outweigh the benefits.

The Surveillance Camera On Your Street Corner: Lawful Spying Or Constitutionally Problematic?

"If you use this inappropriately or if it gets hacked, and it's a national security risk by a foreign actor, it could very quickly snowball and become something that outweighs all of the positives that have incurred up to that point," Carr told Fox News Digital.

"Or, Heaven forbid, you get a government that starts acting totalitarian," he continued. "And then they have the infrastructure in place, and you can't really get rid of it once it's there."

More than 135,000 ALPRs have been identified throughout the country, with roughly four of every five cameras belonging to Flock, according to data from DeFlock.org.

Flock's website says the company has operational cameras — which sit perched atop roadside poles — in 49 states, with each one capturing a vehicle's characteristics and license plate number as it passes.

Teens Accused Of Destroying Flock Camera Until Battery Exploded, Igniting Fire Near Homes: Report

The company insists the cameras do not record continuously or utilize facial recognition technology to identify individuals in a specific car. Its website adds that customers own the data in which Flock gathers and "every search requires a documented reason and is logged for review."

However, instances of police officers using the technology to track previous romantic partners have made headlines in recent months, with some concerned citizens taking matters into their own hands by covering the cameras or shooting them with guns.

Last month, NPR reported that Flock cameras have been vandalized in at least 36 states throughout the country, further fueling the debate surrounding if the technology is truly welcome in the communities in which they were placed.

License Plate Cameras At Home Depot And Lowe's Spark Privacy Fears

Flock did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

The company's use of artificial intelligence continues to be a sticking point for critics of the cameras, with both Republicans and Democrats speaking out against the rollout of Flock's technology.

"I mean, this has probably been one of the most unifying things that I've seen in my lifetime," Carr said, adding, "It's not really a left or right issue, because I think the one thing that people really understand innately, even if they're not expressing it, is that they wouldn't trust their worst enemy with the technology."

The skepticism has been echoed by political leaders on both sides of the aisle.

Click Here For More Coverage Of Media And Culture

Republican Texas Gov. Greg Abbott last week paused state funding for Flock cameras. In Florida, Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis warned against expanding a "digital AI surveillance state," and the state's Department of Transportation announced Monday that it was revoking existing permits for automated license plate readers within state highway rights-of-way.

Democratic Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro also hit back against the company, announcing he would encourage a bipartisan bill for an overall ban on Flock cameras throughout the state.

"We need to work together," Carr told Fox News Digital. "It doesn't matter who's pulling with us on this. We need to work together and make sure that our descendants aren't spied on forever."
